title: Deep learning with interactive segmentation for risk stratification of cystic renal lesions on tri-phase CT: a multicenter study.
abstract: Background Accurate preoperative risk stratification of cystic renal lesions (CRLs) remains a clinical challenge, primarily due to morphological overlap which often leads to the overtreatment of indolent cysts. To address this, we developed and validated an integrated deep learning framework that combines interactive segmentation with tri-phase CT feature integration to refine malignancy prediction. Methods This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 434 patients with CRLs from four institutions, partitioned into training (n=195), validation (n=100), and external test (n=139) cohorts. The reference standard was histopathological diagnosis or ≥4 years of radiological stability. For volumetric segmentation, we implemented an interactive 'human-in-the-loop' Swin UNETR model. To integrate complementary information across the three CT phases, we then deployed a Tri-Phase-Channel (TPC) Perceiver architecture to integrate features extracted by parallel SEResNet50 backbones from unenhanced, corticomedullary, and nephrographic CT phases. Diagnostic performance was evaluated against the single-phase SEResNet50 models and the Bosniak classification version 2019 using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA). Results In the external test cohort, the interactive segmentation model yielded a Dice score of 0.890. For malignancy prediction, the TPC-Perceiver attained an AUC of 0.969 (95% CI: 0.911-1.000), significantly outperforming the Bosniak classification version 2019 (AUC 0.884; p =0.016 ). At the fixed probability threshold of 0.5, the model achieved a sensitivity of 94.4% and a specificity of 96.7%, compared with 100.0% and 76.9%, respectively, for the clinical standard. Furthermore, decision curve analysis indicated that the deep learning framework conferred greater net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. Conclusion The integrated framework showed favorable performance for cystic renal lesion risk stratification. Exploratory pairwise AUC comparisons favored the TPC Perceiver over the single-phase models and the clinical Bosniak v2019 assessment, while its AUC was comparable to that of the previous SETD model. The sensitivity-specificity profile observed at the fixed threshold suggests potential value in reducing false-positive risk stratification. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required before clinical implementation.

title: Multimodal radiomics based on dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound for predicting cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma with Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to develop and validate a multimodal predictive model by integrating radiomic features from B-mode ultrasound (BMUS) and dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound (DCE-US) parametric imaging, as well as clinical and conventional ultrasound features, for preoperative prediction of cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) complicated with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). Methods A total of 191 patients with pathologically confirmed HT-complicated PTC were retrospectively enrolled between December 2023 and July 2025. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n=133) and a validation set (n=58) at a 7:3 ratio using a random number generator. Radiomic features were extracted from BMUS images and DCE-US peak enhancement parametric maps. Feature stability was assessed using intraclass and interclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Key features were selected through a sequential process including the Mann-Whitney U test, recursive feature elimination (RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by calculation of the radiomics score (Rad-score). Independent predictors of CLNM were identified using multivariate logistic regression incorporating clinical and ultrasound features. Three predictive models were constructed: a clinical-ultrasound model, a radiomics model, and a combined multi-modal model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis. Results TG-Ab, TR-Ab, extrathyroidal extension, filling defects, BMUS Rad-score, and DCE-US Rad-score were independent predictors of CLNM (P < 0.05). In the training and validation sets, the combined model achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.936 and 0.916, respectively, which were significantly higher than those of the radiomics model (AUC = 0.825, 0.876) and the clinical-ultrasound model (AUC = 0.760, 0.800; DeLong test, P < 0.05). Calibration curves showed good model fitting. DCA confirmed that the combined model provided greater clinical net benefit. NRI and IDI verified that the combined model significantly improved CLNM prediction performance. SHAP analysis revealed that DCE-US Rad-score was the most important predictor for CLNM. Conclusion A multi-modal predictive model combining dual-modality ultrasound radiomic scores (BMUS and DCE-US) with clinical and ultrasound features can effectively and robustly predict CLNM in patients with HT-complicated PTC and performs better than single-modal models. This model provides an objective reference for the formulation of individualized surgical strategies.

title: IVIM-based habitat imaging for non-invasive assessment of Ki-67 proliferation status in cervical cancer.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate whether voxel-level IVIM-based habitat analysis supports exploratory pretreatment stratification of Ki-67 proliferation status in cervical cancer. Materials and methods Between January 2019 and June 2025, medical records of 149 patients with histopathologically confirmed cervical cancer were initially screened. Before image-quality assessment, 49 were excluded because IVIM MRI had been performed after chemoradiotherapy (n = 5), cervical biopsy sampling (n = 21), or lesion excision (n = 10), or because no pathological Ki-67 immunohistochemistry result was available (n = 13). Of the remaining 100 patients, 17 were excluded because of severe image artefacts (n = 11) or lesions too small for reliable ROI delineation (n = 6), leaving 83 patients for analysis. Patients were stratified into high Ki-67 (Ki-67 >70%, n = 38) and low/equal Ki-67 (Ki-67 ≤70%, n = 45) groups. Solid-tumour regions were analysed with patient-level K-means clustering using normalised D, f, and ADC features; D* was excluded from clustering because of voxel-level fitting instability. Habitat labels were harmonised according to quantitative parameter profiles and treated as image-defined phenotypes. Habitat-derived features, conventional ROI parameters, and logistic models were evaluated for Ki-67 stratification. Results Hab1 ADC was lower in the high- than in the low/equal-Ki-67 group (median [Q1-Q3], 0.947 [0.862-1.161] vs. 1.257 [1.113-1.455] × 10 -3 mm 2 /s; P < 0.001; BH q = 2.04×10 -6 ), whereas Hab3 volume proportion was higher (0.396 [0.341-0.488] vs. 0.279 [0.190-0.390]; P = 0.002; BH q = 0.006). Hab1 ADC outperformed conventional ROI ADC for identifying high Ki-67 status [AUC, 0.826 (95% CI, 0.726-0.909) vs. 0.563 (95% CI, 0.429-0.695); paired DeLong P < 0.001]. The combined Hab1 ADC and Hab3 volume proportion model showed the numerically highest discrimination (apparent AUC, 0.877; 95% CI, 0.794-0.938), but this numerical improvement over Hab1 ADC alone was not statistically significant (paired DeLong P = 0.056). Fixed-feature leave-one-out validation of the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.855 (95% CI, 0.771-0.923) and a Brier score of 0.157 (95% CI, 0.112-0.204). Conclusion IVIM-based habitat analysis showed exploratory potential for non-invasive Ki-67 stratification by isolating a low-diffusivity imaging compartment otherwise obscured by conventional whole-tumour averaging. The combined habitat model should be interpreted as a research-stage imaging biomarker, not a clinical decision tool, and requires prospective external validation before clinical translation.

title: A multimodal deep learning radiomics nomogram integrating clinicopathological features for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant therapy in triple-negative breast cancer: a multicenter retrospective study.
abstract: Background Accurate noninvasive estimation of pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) may support multidisciplinary discussions, but multimodal MRI-ultrasound evidence remains limited. We developed and externally validated a clinicopathological deep learning radiomics nomogram and explored its potential auxiliary value in a strictly hypothetical post-hoc surgical-planning scenario. Methods With institutional review-board approval and waived consent, this retrospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study included 436 biopsy-proven TNBC patients who underwent NAT and surgery: Center 1 training cohort (n = 268) and internal validation cohort (n = 86), plus historical cases from cooperating Centers 2-3 for external validation (n = 82). pCR was defined as ypT0/is ypN0. Pretreatment dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)/apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and B-mode ultrasound were analyzed. Intratumoral and 5-mm peritumoral ring radiomics features were extracted and selected by LASSO. DenseNet-121 extracted modality-specific deep features, fused using multi-head self-attention. Age, tumor size, Ki-67, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), cT/N stage, and histological grade were integrated with imaging scores in a logistic-regression nomogram. Parameters and thresholds were locked after Center 1 development and applied once to external data. No model output was used clinically. Feature standardization and ComBat harmonization parameters were strictly locked to the training cohort before application to validation data. Results pCR occurred in 182/436 patients (41.7%). The nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.917 (95% CI, 0.881-0.947) in training, 0.883 (0.814-0.937) in internal validation, and 0.856 (0.773-0.921) in external validation, exceeding clinical (external AUC, 0.721), radiomics (0.786), and deep learning (0.819) models. External sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy at the locked threshold were 0.765, 0.813, and 0.793, respectively. Calibration was acceptable (slope, 0.93; intercept, -0.06; Brier score, 0.16). Decision curve analysis showed net benefit for thresholds of 0.20-0.70. Multi-threshold analysis revealed that a high-specificity threshold (0.65) yielded a positive predictive value of 0.85, potentially identifying a subset of patients with very high confidence of achieving pCR. Compared with the clinical model, external reclassification improved (continuous net reclassification improvement [NRI], 0.34; integrated discrimination improvement [IDI], 0.11; P = 0.003 and P = 0.008, respectively). Conclusion Among the few multicenter TNBC studies combining MRI, ultrasound, intratumoral/peritumoral radiomics, and attention-based deep learning, this nomogram showed good retrospective accuracy for pCR prediction after NAT. The model is presented as an aid for pCR prediction and preoperative stratification rather than as direct support for surgical decision-making. Prospective validation and clinical-impact studies are required before implementation.

title: Vascular habitat analysis using dynamic susceptibility contrast-enhanced perfusion MRI for differentiating glioblastoma from solitary brain metastases.
abstract: Objective To investigate tumor vascular habitat parameters based on dynamic susceptibility contrast-enhanced perfusion-weighted imaging (DSC-PWI) for differentiating glioblastoma (GBM) from solitary brain metastasis (SBM). Methods In this single-center retrospective study, imaging data from 141 patients with pathologically or clinically confirmed malignant brain tumors (74 GBM, 67 SBM) were analyzed. The hemodynamic tissue signature (HTS) method was used to segment the lesions and construct four tumor vascular habitats: high angiogenic tumor (HAT), low angiogenic tumor (LAT), potentially infiltrated peripheral edema (IPE), and vasogenic peripheral edema (VPE). Pearson correlation analysis was used to quantify the correlations among habitat hemodynamic parameters. Habitat characteristic parameters were calculated, and ROC were plotted to evaluate the diagnostic performance. A nomogram model was constructed using logistic regression. Results GBM exhibited significantly higher median relative cerebral blood volume (rCBV median ) and median relative cerebral blood flow (rCBF median ) than SBM across all four habitat regions (all p < 0.001). In terms of volumetric parameters, the ratio of IPE volume to peritumoral volume ( V (IPE) / V (P) ) was significantly higher in the GBM group ( p < 0.001). Among individual habitat parameters, LAT rCBF median showed the best diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.786 (95% CI: 0.709-0.850). In the GBM group, the perfusion parameters of the IPE and VPE were significantly positively correlated with those of the HAT, whereas no such correlation was found in the SBM group. A nomogram incorporating lesion location, enhancement pattern, and LAT-rCBF median yielded an AUC of 0.857 (95% CI: 0.79-0.92) for distinguishing GBM from SBM, with good calibration. Conclusion Tumor vascular habitat parameters based on DSC-PWI demonstrate significant differences between newly diagnosed GBM and SBM, and the nomogram shows certain value in differentiating between the two tumor types.

title: Artificial intelligence in image-guided cervical interventional radiotherapy: a systematic review.
abstract: Background Imaging-guided interventional radiotherapy (IG-IRT) is the standard of care for locally advanced cervical cancer but remains time-consuming and operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to improve efficiency and reproducibility. Methods A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between 2010 and 2026 investigating AI-based imaging applications in cervical IRT. Eligible studies included original research evaluating segmentation (targets and organ at risk), planning, reconstruction, image registration and applicator selection. Results Fifty-two studies were included. Deep learning-based segmentation showed variable performance across anatomical structures and studies, with Dice coefficients approaching or exceeding 0.90 for some organs at risk and target volumes in the best-performing models. Individual studies reported shorter processing times, reduced contouring variability, accurate applicator reconstruction, and potential support for applicator selection. However, the substantial methodological and clinical heterogeneity precluded direct comparisons among AI approaches. Conclusions The available studies suggest that AI may support the automation of selected workflow steps and assist treatment-related decision-making in image-guided cervical interventional radiotherapy. title: Dosimetric benefits of deep inspiration breath-hold in postoperative radiotherapy for left-sided breast cancer after breast-conserving surgery: an anatomical parameter-based analysis.
abstract: Objective To investigate the dosimetric impact of deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH) technique on radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery for left-sided breast cancer, and to explore the relationship between patient anatomical characteristics and dosimetric benefits of DIBH, providing preliminary evidence for understanding individual differences in DIBH related dosimetric gains and their personalized application. Methods This retrospective study included 17 patients who underwent postoperative radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery for left-sided breast cancer. All patients underwent computed tomography (CT) simulation under both DIBH and free-breathing (FB) conditions, and intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) plans were generated from both image sets. With identical prescription doses and planning optimization objectives, dosimetric parameters for the left lung, heart, and cardiac substructures were compared between the two respiratory conditions. Correlations of the maximum cardiac margin distance (MCMD), cardiac displacement, cardiac displacement volume, heart-to-breast distance (HBD), and changes in lung volume with dosimetric parameters were also analyzed. Results Compared with FB, DIBH significantly reduced the mean dose (Dmean), V20, and V30 of the left lung, as well as the cardiac Dmean, V20, V30, and V40 (all P < 0.05). In addition, DIBH significantly reduced the mean doses to of the right ventricle (RV), left ventricle (LV), and left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) compared with FB (all P < 0.05). Correlation analysis demonstrated that MCMD under the DIBH condition was positively correlated with cardiac Dmean. The change in MCMD between DIBH and FB was negatively correlated with cardiac and ventricular dose parameters. Cardiac displacement volume between the two respiratory states was positively correlated with changes in mean heart dose. Further analysis revealed that changes in lung volume were positively correlated with cardiac displacement along the Z-axis and changes in HBD while negatively correlated with LAD Dmean under the DIBH condition. Conclusion DIBH can reduce radiation exposure to the left lung, heart, and selected cardiac substructures while satisfying target-dose requirements. Exploratory analyses indicated that cardiac geometric parameters and changes in lung volume were associated with selected dosimetric parameters, suggesting that dynamic anatomical changes during DIBH may help explain interindividual differences in dosimetric benefit. These findings require further validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

title: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumor of the kidney with prominent peritumoral adipose tissue: a case report radiologically mimicking angiomyolipoma with epithelial cysts.
abstract: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumor of the kidney (MEST) is a rare renal neoplasm with biphasic differentiation comprising epithelial and stromal components. It typically appears as a mixed cystic-solid mass on imaging, and the prognosis is favorable in the vast majority of cases. We report a case of MEST with a prominent fat component on imaging: a 54-year-old woman was admitted with a 1-month history of left flank distension and pain. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed a mixed cystic-solid mass at the lower pole of the left kidney, with a prominent low-attenuation fat-density area surrounding the mass. Preoperatively, the lesion was considered an unusual angiomyolipoma with epithelial cysts (AMLEC). Because the lesion was small, located at the lower pole, and relatively well circumscribed, the patient underwent laparoscopic left partial nephrectomy. Postoperative histopathologic examination confirmed that the left renal mass was benign; however, immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrated positivity for EMA and PCK in the epithelial component and for PR and ER in the stromal component, supporting a diagnosis of MEST. The adipose tissue submitted separately with the tumor was located around the tumor and could not be definitively confirmed as an intratumoral component. This case demonstrates that MEST may also exhibit prominent adipose tissue on imaging and illustrates the diagnostic pitfall in which fat-related imaging findings cause MEST to mimic AMLEC, making the early distinction between MEST and cystic change in fat-containing renal tumors challenging.

title: Retroauricular approach for carotid body tumor resection: a case report.
abstract: Introduction Carotid body tumors (CBTs) are rare and highly vascular paragangliomas arising at the carotid bifurcation. Surgical resection remains the standard treatment for CBTs. However, the conventional transcervical approach inevitably leaves a visible cervical scar, which may negatively affect quality of life in patients with cosmetic concerns. Case presentation A 27-year-old woman presented with a progressively enlarging right neck mass over a 6-month period. Ultrasonography demonstrated a hypervascular lesion surrounding the carotid arteries, and fine-needle aspiration was avoided because of the vascular nature of the tumor. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 4-cm enhancing mass at the carotid bifurcation, highly suggestive of a CBT. Because the patient expressed concern regarding a visible cervical scar, a retroauricular approach was selected after thorough discussion of its potential risks and benefits. The operation was performed by a head and neck surgeon with intraoperative assistance from a vascular surgeon. Complete tumor resection was successfully achieved despite the need for repair of two small arterial defects encountered during tumor mobilization. The operative time was 300 minutes, and the estimated blood loss was 900 mL. The postoperative course was uneventful, and no major complications or tumor recurrence were observed during 12 months of follow-up. The patient reported satisfaction with the cosmetic outcome, although no objective cosmetic assessment was performed. Conclusion In carefully selected patients with Shamblin type I or II CBT, the retroauricular approach may represent a feasible hidden-scar alternative to the conventional transcervical approach.

title: Ultrasonic manifestations of diffuse pericardial mesothelioma masquerading as pericardial effusion: a case report.
abstract: Background Primary pericardial mesothelioma (PPM) is an exceedingly rare, highly invasive cardiac neoplasm with insidious onset and non-specific clinical symptoms. Due to the lack of typical early manifestations and effective routine diagnostic methods, PPM is often misdiagnosed and missed, resulting in delayed treatment and poor prognosis. Case presentation A 42-year-old male presented with 6 months of recurrent chest tightness and pain, worsening over 2 months, and two prior admissions for unexplained pericardial effusion. On admission, he had tachycardia, distant heart sounds, bilateral lower extremity edema, and a 3×2 cm hard, fixed left supraclavicular lymph node. Imaging confirmed pericardial effusion with abnormal pericardial lesions. Ultrasound-guided pericardiocentesis yielded only a small amount of red jelly-like material, with cytology suggesting epithelioid neoplastic cells. Supraclavicular lymph node biopsy confirmed metastatic malignant mesothelioma. Nivolumab immunotherapy showed no improvement. Pericardial tumor resection revealed diffuse, fish-flesh-like tumor invading the myocardium and great vessels. Final pathology confirmed epithelioid-type PPM. Conclusion Patients with recurrent unexplained pericardial effusion and atypical sonographic features, such as flocculent echoes and irregular pericardial thickening, should raise suspicion for PPM. Early recognition of these signs and timely pathological confirmation are critical to avoid diagnostic delays and may improve outcomes.

title: Radiologist-guided multimodal fusion network for differentiating parotid tumors on 3D non-contrast CT.
abstract: Objectives To improve the diagnostic accuracy of benign versus malignant parotid tumors using non-contrast CT. We propose a clinician-in-the-loop hybrid framework that mitigates low soft-tissue contrast by fusing semi-automated 3D visual features with expert semantic descriptors. Methods This multi-center retrospective study analyzed non-contrast CTs from 367 patients. We developed AttenNet, a semi-automated model. First, an nnU-Net module automates 3D tumor segmentation, eliminating manual bounding boxes. A 3D-ResNet backbone then extracts volumetric features, which are dynamically fused with radiologist-provided semantic labels via a Multi-Head Cross-Attention Fusion (MHAF) mechanism. This allows the network to query visual morphology based on expert priors. Diagnostic performance and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) interpretability were evaluated. Results The segmentation achieved a median Dice of 0.827. AttenNet (3D-ResNet) yielded an AUC of 0.908, significantly outperforming the image-only 3D-ResNet (AUC: 0.741) and expert-feature models (AUC: 0.821). External validation ( n = 20) reached an AUC of 0.560-0.910.However, given the extremely small sample size, these results must be interpreted strictly as an exploratory proof-of-concept rather than definitive confirmation of generalizability. Grad-CAM confirmed that AttenNet highlights clinically essential geometric indicators-specifically tumor margins and internal heterogeneity-for differentiating malignancy, whereas single-modality baselines focused on background artifacts. Conclusion This clinician-in-the-loop paradigm successfully integrates spatial imaging with expert reasoning. While multimodal fusion drove the primary performance gains, the MHAF mechanism provided enhanced spatial interpretability.

title: Non-invasive preoperative MRI-based deep transfer learning radiomics model for predicting meningioma brain invasion.
abstract: Background Current preoperative assessment of meningioma brain invasion (BI) demands imaging analytical frameworks that optimize computational efficiency while capturing multidimensional tumor-pathology correlations. Building upon the inherent advantages of 2.5D MRI in synthesizing multiplanar biological data with manageable processing loads, this study innovatively integrates deep transfer learning (DTL), a technique bridging pretrained network knowledge with target domain adaptation, to systematically identify tumor-invasive biological signatures and develop an optimized predictive system using preoperative contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI). Methods This retrospective study enrolled 674 patients with pathologically confirmed meningiomas, including 53 with BI and 621 without BI. The cohort was stratified into a training set and an independent test set. Tumor regions of interest (ROIs) were delineated on CE-T1WI, and radiomics and DTL features were extracted. Radiomics and DTL features were fused via early fusion, followed by feature selection. Within the training cohort, five-fold cross-validation was performed, with SMOTE applied exclusively to the training portion of each fold; validation folds and the independent test set retained their original class distributions. Results The effectiveness of the models was compared using the area under the ROC curve (AUC). In the training set, ComM achieved an AUC of 0.977, while in the test set, its AUC reached 0.935. ComM demonstrated the best performance (training set: AUCComM > AUCDTLRM > AUCRadM > AUCClinM > AUCDTLM; test set: AUCComM > AUCDTLRM > AUCRadM > AUCDTLM > AUCClinM), showing excellent preoperative predictive capability for meningioma BI. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated good model fit, and the calibration curve revealed that ComM was closest to the ideal curve. Conclusion ClinM, RadM, DTLM, DTLRM, and ComM based on 2.5D CE-T1WI all exhibited good performance in predicting meningioma BI. The clinical-radiomics-DTL fusion model (ComM) demonstrated the highest efficacy, suggesting that DTL provides additional features correlated with meningioma BI that differ from radiomics features. This model shows potential clinical utility for preoperative prediction; however, further external validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

title: Multiparametric MRI-based habitat and peritumoral radiomics integrating semi-automated segmentation for preoperative prediction of high-grade prostate cancer: a dual-center study.
abstract: Background This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning framework that combines semi-automated segmentation, intratumoral habitats derived from multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), and multiscale peritumoral radiomics to predict high-grade prostate cancer (HGPCa) before surgery. Methods This retrospective dual-center study involved 274 patients, comprising 208 from Center 1 for development and 66 from Center 2 for external test. The clinical and imaging variables included patient age, serum PSA, fPSA, PSAD, maximum tumor diameter, PI-RADS scores, and anatomical zone distribution (PZ vs. TZ). The development cohort was randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 145) and an internal validation cohort (n = 63). Intratumoral habitats were delineated using semi-automated segmentation and unsupervised K-means clustering, while peritumoral radiomic features were extracted from concentric 1-, 3-, and 5-mm shells. Predictive classifiers were optimized through machine learning algorithms, particularly a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for the habitat signature. A combined clinical-radiomics nomogram was constructed, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) employed to enhance model interpretability. Subgroup analyses were performed to assess the discriminative performance of the combined nomogram across the peripheral zone (PZ) and transition zone (TZ). title: Liquid biopsy using circulating miRNAs for the identification of recurrence-associated biomarkers in glioblastoma CNS WHO grade 4.
abstract: Introduction Glioblastoma CNS WHO Grade 4 (GBM) is associated with poor prognosis and high recurrence rates despite the current therapeutic approaches. Conventional imaging, in particular Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), is primarily used during follow-up to detect tumor recurrence but has limited ability to distinguish recurrence from therapy-related changes, such as tissue necrosis and postoperative scar tissue. Liquid biopsy using circulating tumor-specific serological biomarkers, such as miRNAs, provides a gene expression signature for early identification of GBM recurrence. This pilot "proof-of-concept" study investigated the potential of circulating tumor-derived miRNA in whole blood samples for early detection of tumor recurrence. Methods In a previous whole-transcriptome screening (NGS) study, whole-blood samples (n = 33) from seven patients and tumor biopsies (n = 4) were used to identify biomarkers. Corresponding to tumor surgery and recurrence, miRNA expression was examined in pre-surgical blood samples and tumor tissues. In whole blood, we investigated whether a pattern could be identified indicating post-surgery downregulation, consistent with reduced tumor burden, followed by a return to pre-surgery levels at recurrence. We identified 1-19 miRNA species per patient (a total of 72 miRNAs) showing this pattern. In this manuscript, we present the qRT-PCR validation results. The 45 most promising miRNAs identified by NGS study were selected and quantified using qRT-PCR. In addition, miR-21 was included as a promising candidate reported in the literature. To address challenges in miRNA normalization, five normalization strategies and unnormalized raw Ct values were compared. Results Two normalization approaches (median DCt normalization and unnormalized raw Ct values) showed no systematic bias. Depending on the normalization method, the agreement between NGS and qRT-PCR ranged from 23.6 to 27.9%. Although the concordance between NGS and qRT-PCR was low at the individual-patient level, qRT-PCR identified a common set of 24 miRNAs differentially regulated across patients. Notably, miR-424-3p and miR-362-5p were shared by five of seven patients, followed by miR-1307-3p and miR-22-5p , each shared by four patients. Interestingly, miR-21 did not show the predefined recurrence-associated pattern in any patient. Discussion Blood-based miRNA profiling may complement imaging in longitudinal monitoring of GBM patients, although clinical benefits have not been confirmed, and validation in a larger independent cohort is required.

title: Macroscopic versus rapid on-site evaluation for EUS-guided tissue acquisition of solid pancreatic masses: a systematic review, diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis, and network meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition (EUS-TA) is central to the pathological diagnosis of solid pancreatic masses, but the comparative value of rapid on-site cytologic evaluation (ROSE), macroscopic on-site evaluation (MOSE), and no on-site evaluation (NONE) may vary by needle type and remains uncertain. Methods We performed a PRISMA-DTA systematic review registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251241446). Potential cohort overlap and data dependency were assessed before quantitative synthesis. Diagnostic 2 × 2 data were synthesized with a bivariate binomial-normal random-effects model. Independent direct comparisons were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis for correct versus incorrect diagnosis, with complementary absolute differences in sensitivity and specificity. An exploratory three-node network meta-analysis (NMA) compared ROSE, MOSE, and NONE. Results Thirty-one eligible reports contributed 67 strategy-specific diagnostic datasets. After excluding 21 duplicate, nested, paired, or otherwise dependent datasets, 46 independent datasets representing 4,901 arm-level observations were included in the primary DTA. Pooled sensitivity was 0.94 (95% CI 0.92-0.95) and specificity was 1.00 (0.98-1.00); Deeks' asymmetry test was positive (P <0.001). In direct comparisons, ROSE improved composite diagnostic accuracy versus NONE in FNA studies (OR 5.56, 95% CI 1.76-17.62; k = 4), but not in FNB studies (OR 1.08, 0.42-2.79; k = 4); the FNA-versus-FNB interaction was exploratory (P = 0.012). MOSE versus NONE in FNB was uncertain (OR 1.31, 0.60-2.87; k = 4), as was MOSE versus ROSE (OR 1.53, 0.05-49.13; k = 3). The exploratory NMA did not identify a statistically clear difference for ROSE versus NONE (OR 1.67, 0.94-2.95), MOSE versus NONE (OR 1.89, 0.86-4.20), or MOSE versus ROSE (OR 1.14, 0.48-2.71). Conclusions EUS-TA showed high overall diagnostic performance. ROSE may add value in FNA-era workflows, whereas a clear incremental benefit was not detected with FNB. MOSE remains a plausible resource-sparing strategy, but comparative estimates are imprecise. The NMA should be regarded as hypothesis-generating because of sparse comparisons, methodological heterogeneity, small-study effects, and low-to-very-low certainty. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251241446.

title: Primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma with brain metastases in a male: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma (PPC) is an exceptionally rare and highly aggressive extragonadal trophoblastic malignancy in males, with no established standard treatment. Cytotoxic chemotherapy alone generally yields limited therapeutic benefit, while the role of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains poorly defined. Here, we report a 41-year-old man who presented with a six-month history of cough and was found to have a large right upper lobe pulmonary mass with multiple brain metastases. Histopathological examination revealed typical trophoblastic differentiation, and immunohistochemistry demonstrated diffuse positivity for HCG, CK7, GATA3, and SALL4, whereas TTF-1 and Napsin A were negative. Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-HCG) was markedly elevated (> 10, 000 mIU/mL), and no gonadal primary lesion was identified, confirming the diagnosis of primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma. The patient underwent multimodal treatment including radiotherapy, EMA/CO chemotherapy, EMA/EP combined with sintilimab, and third-line therapy consisting of nab-paclitaxel, bevacizumab, and penpulimab. Despite intensive treatment, the disease progressed rapidly with new intracranial and systemic metastases. Throughout the disease course, serial β-HCG measurements closely paralleled radiographic findings and provided timely guidance for therapeutic decision-making. In addition, we reviewed previously reported metastatic male PPC cases and performed an exploratory survival analysis, which suggested that patients receiving ICI-based therapy tended to have longer overall survival than those treated without immunotherapy. Although these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size, this case highlights the highly aggressive nature of male PPC, emphasizes the diagnostic and monitoring value of dynamic β-HCG assessment, and supports further investigation of chemoimmunotherapy as a potential treatment strategy for this rare malignancy.

title: Imaging biomarkers related to 18F-FDG PET/CT for predicting microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction This study, through a meta-analysis, aimed to assess the predictive performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) for microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library were comprehensively searched from database inception to January 13, 2026. EndNote 21was employed for literature screening and data extraction. Meta-analysis was carried out on the extracted data using Stata 15, MetaDisc 1.4, and MedCalc. Results In total, 21 studies were included, involving 2,023 patients with HCC, of whom 890 were MVI+ and 1,133 were MVI-. In univariable analyses, both tumor-to-normal liver uptake ratio (TLR) (odds ratio [OR] = 2.577, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.446-4.593, P = 0.001) and maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) (OR = 1.272, 95% CI: 1.036-1.561, P = 0.021) were significantly associated with an increased MVI risk. After multivariable adjustment, SUVmax retained independent predictive value (OR = 2.140, 95% CI: 1.244-3.681, P = 0.006), whereas the multivariable evidence for TLR was derived from a single study and required further validation. AUC values for SUVmax and radiomics score (Rad-score) were 0.819 (95% CI: 0.739-0.899) and 0.809 (95% CI: 0.762-0.857), respectively, with relatively balanced values for sensitivity, specificity, and negative likelihood ratio. Conclusion The available evidence supports SUVmax as one of the metabolic markers for preoperative MVI risk assessment in HCC, with Rad-score similar to SUVmax in diagnostic discrimination. The complementary value of the two markers was not demonstrated by this Meta-analysis, but rather derived from inferences proposed by external studies. Moreover, because the included radiomics studies did not report a pooled effect size for the combined model integrating SUVmax and Rad-score, a Meta-analysis targeting this model is currently not feasible. Therefore, the complementarity of SUVmax and Rad-score should be regarded as a hypothesis to be tested. In the future, multicenter, prospective radiomics studies with rigorous external validation are warranted to further explore a combined prediction model based on SUVmax and Rad-score. On this basis, an integrated assessment workflow should be gradually established, by which preoperative decisions are guided. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261289724.

title: A prospective pilot study of urine microRNA as a biomarker of urinary radiation toxicity following MRI-guided prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy.
abstract: Introduction Urinary toxicities are common following prostate radiotherapy and can impair quality of life. New biomarkers are needed that can predict the risk of urinary toxicity following MRI guided stereotactic body radiotherapy (MR-SBRT) to assist with selection of the most appropriate radiotherapy treatment approach. We aimed to identify urine miRNA biomarkers of radiation-induced urinary toxicities. Methods Ten patients undergoing MR-SBRT were enrolled on a prospective biorepository protocol and urine specimens were collected before, at the final fraction and 2-4 months following radiotherapy. RNA was isolated and microRNA sequencing was performed followed by qPCR for confirmation of microRNA expression changes. Differences in microRNA expression were assessed with regard to timepoint, cancer risk category and urinary toxicity. Results Both sequencing and qPCR showed that expressions of miR-26a-5p and miR-95-3p decrease during MR-SBRT and increase during early follow up. miR-204-3p and miR-192-5p changed differently in patients with and without urinary radiation toxicity. Expression of miR-375-3p was lower in patients with higher risk category (NCCN unfavorable intermediate to high risk or recurrent/metastatic) at all timepoints and decreased during and after MR-SBRT, especially in patients with a lower risk category (NCCN low to favorable intermediate risk) of prostate cancer. Discussion Urine microRNA analysis is feasible and may identify biomarkers linked to radiation-induced urinary toxicity and prostate cancer severity. The findings of this pilot study are limited by the sample size and should be prospectively validated.

title: Relevance between patients' clinical factors and 4D-CT lung ventilation heterogeneity for evaluating the adoption of functional avoidance thoracic radiotherapy with a large patient database.
abstract: Objective Four-dimensional computed tomography (4D-CT)-guided functional-avoidance radiotherapy reduces radiation pneumonitis, but the lack of patient selection criteria limits its adoption. This study aimed to identify clinical predictors of lung ventilation heterogeneity and determine which patients derive the greatest dosimetric benefit from functional-avoidance planning. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 274 lung cancer patients. 4D-CT ventilation imaging was generated via deformable registration and a density-change algorithm, and the coefficient of variation (CoV) across six lung zones quantified heterogeneity. Clinical factors were assessed using Mann-Whitney U, Spearman, and multivariable logistic regression for three ventilation outcomes. Thirty-two patients were selected from CoV quartiles and re-planned with functional-avoidance plans; dosimetric parameters were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction applied to address multiple comparisons. Results Univariate analysis showed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and airway obstruction reduced bilateral mean ventilation, while central tumors impaired ipsilateral ventilation. Higher CoV was observed in stage III-IV versus I-II, central versus peripheral tumors, and patients with airway obstruction. Multivariable analysis identified airway obstruction as an independent predictor of elevated CoV (adjusted OR = 2.914, 95% CI: 1.315-6.454, P<0.05). Central location and advanced stage showed borderline significance, while COPD trended toward lower CoV. Dosimetrically, functional-avoidance plans reduced functional lung metrics in a heterogeneity-dependent manner. After FDR correction, key metrics (fMLD, fV10, fV20, fV30) remained significant in Group 1 (highest CoV; Q = 0.040-0.049), while significance diminished in lower CoV groups. Leave-one-out (LOO) sensitivity analysis confirmed fMLD and fV20 as robust endpoints. Furthermore, beam arrangement modifications were most frequent in Group 1 (5/8 patients) and absent in Group 4 (0/8), reflecting clinical optimization needs rather than confounding. Conclusions Ventilation heterogeneity is driven by tumor burden and airway patency. Patients with advanced stage, central tumors, or airway obstruction exhibit the strongest heterogeneity and may represent appropriate candidates for functional-avoidance radiotherapy in future prospective trials. However, as this replanning study lacked clinical follow-up for radiation pneumonitis, these findings reflect dosimetric rather than confirmed clinical patient-level benefit. Notably, CoV quartiles were derived from internal median splits within this cohort and require external validation. This study provides a dosimetric basis for hypothesis-generating patient selection.

title: CBCT-based adaptive radiotherapy and automated radiotherapy decision-making systems: development and current status.
abstract: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-based adaptive radiotherapy (ART) has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing inter-fractional anatomical and physiological changes during treatment. By incorporating on-treatment imaging, ART enables treatment plans to be adapted to the anatomy of the day, with the potential to improve target coverage and reduce dose exposure to organs at risk (OARs). However, routine implementation remains constrained by the limited image quality of CBCT, uncertainties in dose calculation, labour-intensive workflows and the lack of reliable criteria for determining when adaptation is clinically necessary. This review summarises the development, current status and future prospects of CBCT-based ART, with particular emphasis on artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted automated delineation and automated radiotherapy decision-making systems. CBCT is widely available on modern linear accelerators and remains the most practical imaging basis for ART in many centres. Nevertheless, poor soft-tissue contrast, noise, artefacts, field-of-view truncation and unstable Hounsfield unit values limit its performance in target delineation and dose reconstruction. Recent advances in image-quality enhancement, deformable image registration and synthetic CT generation have partially addressed these limitations. AI-based auto-segmentation models, including convolutional neural networks, Transformers, generative adversarial networks and diffusion models, have demonstrated increasingly favourable geometric accuracy and workflow efficiency. Automated decision-making systems can advise clinicians whether treatment-plan adaptation is required and how it should be implemented according to each patient's circumstances, representing a prerequisite for more efficient ART. Current research has mainly focused on two approaches: adaptation triggered by predefined dosimetric thresholds, and artificial-intelligence-based models that learn from prior knowledge and predict potential dosimetric changes for the current patient based on previous experience. Both approaches have their respective strengths and limitations, but require further refinement, including the systematic exploration of decision thresholds. Moreover, the realisation of fully automated adaptive radiotherapy will require the integration of additional systems, including automated treatment planning and automated QA. Overall, CBCT-based ART assisted by AI is technically feasible and may improve dosimetric quality and treatment efficiency. Future progress requires improved CBCT-specific algorithms, integrated automated planning and QA, multicentre validation, standardised safety frameworks and stronger evidence of clinical benefit.

title: Multiple sclerosis relapse following gamma knife radiosurgery for meningioma in a patient treated with natalizumab: case report.
abstract: Objectives We describe a case of a patient with multiple sclerosis (MS) stable on natalizumab who developed widespread gadolinium-enhancing lesions and clinical relapse seven and eight months after gamma knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for left cerebellar convexity meningioma. We explore how increased blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability post-GKRS could potentially interfere with the lymphocyte anti-trafficking effect of natalizumab and result in new central nervous system (CNS) inflammation distant from the radiation site. Methods Comprehensive analysis of the patient's chart, brain and spine imaging, serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) profiles was conducted. We compiled a graphical representation of treatment changes, radiologic findings, and GKRS initiation within one timeframe. We conducted a structured literature review to support the discussion of this case and hypothesize possible pathophysiological mechanisms contributing to clinical and radiological findings. Results Seven months after GKRS, follow-up brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multiple gadolinium-enhancing lesions in both cerebral hemispheres, and repeat imaging one month later revealed new gadolinium-enhancing lesions, correlating with the patient's clinical relapse. Alternative causes of disease progression, including radiation-induced demyelination, radionecrosis, opportunistic infections, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), and development of anti-natalizumab antibodies, were explored and considered less likely. The patient was switched to ofatumumab with subsequent clinical and radiological stability. Discussion Given extensive new inflammatory lesions far from the GKRS site, it seems unlikely that the sole mechanism was radiation-induced neurotoxicity. We hypothesize that late delayed radiation side effects caused by GKRS may have enabled peripheral lymphocytes to enter the CNS, counteracting the effects of natalizumab on blocking lymphocyte trafficking through the BBB and possibly contributing to MS relapse.

title: Case Report: Long-term survival in FIGO stage IVB small cell carcinoma of the ovary, pulmonary type following complete cytoreduction and platinum re-challenge.
abstract: Background Small cell carcinoma of the ovary, pulmonary type (SCCOPT), is a rare and highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis. Long-term survival in advanced-stage disease has rarely been reported. Case presentation A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman presented with FIGO stage IVB SCCOPT accompanied by extensive peritoneal carcinomatosis and a solitary liver metastasis. No pulmonary lesion suggestive of primary lung malignancy was identified on CT, PET/CT, or chest radiography. She underwent aggressive primary cytoreductive surgery achieving complete macroscopic resection (R0), followed by four cycles of cisplatin and etoposide (EP). Sixteen months after diagnosis, isolated intracranial recurrence with multiple brain metastases were successfully treated with radiotherapy. Twenty-one months after diagnosis, systemic recurrence involving multiple liver metastases and a spinal metastasis was treated with six cycles of EP re-challenge, resulting in a marked radiologic response and subsequent durable disease control. The patient remained alive without clinical evidence of disease progression at the latest follow-up, 104 months after diagnosis. Conclusions This case suggests that prolonged survival may be achievable in selected patients with advanced SCCOPT through aggressive multimodal treatment. Complete cytoreductive surgery, platinum-based chemotherapy, including EP re-challenge following a prolonged platinum-free interval and previous response to platinum-based chemotherapy, and timely local treatment of metastatic lesions may contribute to durable disease control.

title: HSV-Net: hybrid state-space and self-supervised vision fusion with progressive contour learning for CT pulmonary nodule segmentation.
abstract: Accurate voxel-level segmentation of pulmonary nodules on chest CT is needed for diameter and volume measurement, growth tracking, and quantitative assessment in lung cancer screening. The task remains difficult: nodules vary in attenuation, size, and contact with vessels or pleura, and clinically relevant morphology often lies in a thin, ambiguous margin. Existing systems commonly trade contour fidelity for speed-large prompt-driven foundation models can be accurate but slow, whereas compact CNN or SSM decoders are efficient yet tend to smooth spiculated and ground-glass borders. We propose HSV-Net (Hybrid State-space-Vision Network), a dual-stream 3D network that is prompt-free after nodule localization: an SSM3D stream provides whole-patch context with linear-complexity state-space blocks, and an OrthoLoRA stream adapts frozen DINOv2 features on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. A Hybrid Gated Mixer (HGM) fuses the two streams before FPN decoding, and Progressive Contour Learning (PCL) supervises overlap, signed-distance-field geometry, and uncertainty-weighted contour refinement. On a 10-patient QIN Lung CT/QIN-LungCT-Seg development subset ( n = 12 tumors; nested patient-level 5-fold CV), HSV-Net obtained the highest mean Dice (90.1% ± 1.0%; 95% CI [88.9, 91.3]) and Boundary F1 (86.3% ± 1.3%) among the compared methods on 128 × 128 × 64 patches, with a latency of 58 ms. A standard full-volume nnU-Net v2 baseline reached 88.6% ± 1.0% Dice on the same QIN folds, still below HSV-Net. On an independent LIDC-IDRI benchmark with expert volumetric consensus masks (186 patients/294 nodules; patient-level 5-fold CV within LIDC, not QIN→LIDC transfer), HSV-Net achieved 87.8% ± 1.1% Dice and 83.6% ± 1.3% Boundary F1, outperforming full-volume nnU-Net (87.1% ± 1.0% Dice). LUNA16 was retained only as a proxy size/localization check with diameter-matched spherical references, not as contour external validation.

title: Low CT-derived vertebral attenuation as a prognostic factor in hepatocellular carcinoma patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
abstract: Background Computed tomography (CT)-derived vertebral attenuation has been recognized as an indicator of prognosis for patients undergoing tumor removal, liver transplant, or transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) therapy, but similar research has not been reported in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study aims to explore the prognostic value of CT-derived vertebral attenuation in HCC patients treated with ICIs. Methods This retrospective study included HCC patients who received ICI treatment at Wuhan Union Hospital between July 2020 and March 2024. CT-derived vertebral attenuation was assessed by measuring mean Hounsfield unit (HU) values in the center of the first lumbar vertebra (L1) on non-contrast CT scans. Based on the optimal cutoff value derived from X-tile software, patients were classified into the CT-derived L1 attenuation-low group (≤100 HU) and the CT-derived L1 attenuation-high group (>100 HU). A comparison of the baseline characteristics of the two groups was made, followed by a propensity score matching (PSM) analysis to balance the variables. The objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were calculated for both groups, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox regression models were used to analyze overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Results The cohort consisted of 357 patients, divided into the L1 attenuation-low group (n = 112) and the L1 attenuation-high group (n = 245). Among all patients, 30.0% (107/357) achieved complete or partial response. After PSM analysis, both groups contained 91 patients. The L1 attenuation-low group had shorter OS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15-2.60; P = 0.008) and PFS (HR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.04-2.08; P = 0.030) than the L1 attenuation-high group. Conclusion CT-derived L1 attenuation can stratify survival risk for HCC patients undergoing ICI treatment.

title: Boundary-aware geometric Mamba network for breast tumor segmentation in 3D MRI.
abstract: Introduction Accurate breast tumor segmentation in Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging (DCE-MRI) is important for reliable diagnosis and treatment planning. However, complex tumor morphology, diverse spatial structures, and indistinct boundaries remain challenging for existing segmentation methods. Convolutional neural network-based methods have limited ability to model long-range dependencies, while Transformer-based methods often introduce substantial computational overhead. Although Mamba-based approaches provide an efficient alternative, conventional scanning strategies may suffer from directional bias and insufficiently capture three-dimensional structural variations. Methods We propose a Boundary-Aware Geometric Mamba Network (BAGMNet) for three-dimensional breast tumor segmentation. BAGMNet establishes a structural representation learning framework that combines geometric modeling, multi-directional state-space propagation, and boundary-aware feature refinement. The Geometric Mamba Encoder constructs complementary spatial representations through multiple geometric transformations, while the Multi-directional Selective State Space module enhances three-dimensional dependency modeling and alleviates the directional bias of conventional Mamba scanning. The Gated State-space Fusion and Adaptive Skip Recalibration modules further integrate local structural details with global contextual information and enhance boundary-related representations during feature propagation. Results Extensive experiments were conducted on the ISPY1 and Yunnan breast MRI datasets. BAGMNet achieved Dice scores of 70.34% and 79.14%, with average surface distances of 9.79 mm and 8.96 mm on the ISPY1 and Yunnan datasets, respectively. Compared with representative convolutional neural network-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based methods, BAGMNet achieved competitive performance in both regional segmentation accuracy and boundary localization.

title: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma manifesting as a solitary metastasis to the skeletal muscle of the scapular region accompanied by invasion of the adjacent bone while on PD-1 inhibitor maintenance therapy: a case report.
abstract: Cervical cancer is a common malignancy in women worldwide, with distant metastases frequently occurring in the lungs, liver, bones, and lymph nodes. However, this case report presents an extremely rare isolated metastasis to the left scapular region,specifically located between the supraspinatus and the trapezius muscles, in a patient with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma who developed this lesion during maintenance therapy with a programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) inhibitor after completing concurrent chemoradiotherapy. The clinical presentation of this metastatic lesion was atypical and posed a significant diagnostic challenge; however, multimodal imaging (MRI, PET/CT) and histopathological examination ultimately confirmed the diagnosis of cervical cancer metastasis. This finding underscores the necessity of maintaining a high level of vigilance for metastases in atypical sites, even in the era of immunotherapy. To manage this rare presentation, a multidisciplinary team developed a comprehensive treatment strategy centered on surgical resection, followed by postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy administered concurrently with chemotherapy and anti-angiogenic therapy(Q3W) consisting of paclitaxel 135 mg/m², cisplatin 50 mg/m², and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg. The patient remained recurrence-free at 13 months, suggesting that a multimodal combined local and systemic strategy may be feasible for selected patients with solitary muscle metastasis. This case not only adds to the clinical understanding of rare metastases in cervical cancer but also demonstrates that tumors can still metastasize to atypical sites under immunotherapy. These findings highlight the need for vigilance regarding metastases at atypical sites during immunotherapy. Any underlying mechanism-including immune editing and clonal evolution-remains speculative in the absence of paired molecular data and requires further validation.

title: Case Report: Improvement in neurologic symptoms and remission following non-operative management of locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck following cemiplimab therapy: two cases.
abstract: Background Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma is a common skin malignancy in aging populations. Surgical resection and radiotherapy can result in significant morbidity, as well as functional and cosmetic impairments. PD-1 antibodies are promising treatments for locally advanced disease. Case presentation Two elderly men (aged 71 and 73) with locoregionally advanced head and neck tumors received neoadjuvant treatment with cemiplimab (350 mg IV every 3 weeks). Both patients presented with neurologic symptoms concerning for nerve involvement; however, perineural spread could not be identified radiographically or by limited biopsies. Both patients achieved a significant clinical response after only four doses of cemiplimab. After 4 additional doses, both patients underwent elective treatment discontinuation and surgery and radiotherapy were omitted. With over 12-month follow-up, both patients remained free of recurrence. Treatment was well-tolerated with only Grade 1 pruritus. Conclusion These observations are promising and suggest the feasibility of response-adapted management following cemiplimab therapy in selected patients with advanced squamous cell skin cancer with resolution of neurologic symptoms. This approach may allow for omission of surgery and radiotherapy in selected patients. Further investigation to define appropriate candidates for this approach appears warranted.

title: Cone-beam CT-based synthetic CT generation for adaptive radiotherapy: methodological paradigms, clinical reliability assessment, and translation.
abstract: Synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generated from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) has important applications in quantitative imaging, dose recalculation, and adaptive radiotherapy. Deep learning has improved image quality and Hounsfield unit accuracy, but its reliability for patient-specific dosimetry and routine clinical use remains uncertain. This narrative review examines deep learning methods for generating sCT from treatment CBCT in photon and proton radiotherapy, with emphasis on data requirements, generalizability, structural fidelity, dosimetric accuracy, and clinical feasibility. The literature search was last updated on 30 July 2026. Current methods mainly include supervised regression, adversarial networks, registrationguided approaches, and diffusion models. Available evidence demonstrates encouraging image and dosimetric performance, although no method consistently performs best across anatomical sites, imaging systems, and treatment modalities. Most studies are based on proof of concept or single-center validation and show considerable heterogeneity in datasets, acquisition protocols, reference images, registration methods, and evaluation criteria. External validation, prospective assessment, failure detection, and quality assurance remain limited. Future studies should emphasize multicenter validation, standardized and modality-specific evaluation criteria, uncertainty assessment, and prospective workflow testing. More rigorous and clinically relevant evidence is needed to support the reliable use of sCT in patient-specific adaptive radiotherapy.

title: Case Report: Bilateral vestibulopathy associated with leptomeningeal metastasis.
abstract: Bilateral vestibulopathy (BVP) presents with oscillopsia, unsteadiness, and imbalance. Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is a rare and underrecognized cause of BVP, with direct infiltration of the vestibulocochlear nerves representing a potential mechanism of bilateral vestibular dysfunction. We report a case of LM-related BVP documented by quantitative video head impulse test (vHIT) of all six semicircular canals. A 61-year-old man presented with a six-month history of dizziness, tinnitus, oscillopsia, imbalance, and bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. vHIT showed reduced vestibulo-ocular reflex gain in all six semicircular canals. Contrast-enhanced MRI revealed leptomeningeal enhancement and enhancement of both vestibulocochlear nerves. CSF showed elevated protein, lymphocytic pleocytosis, and malignant cells. Serum anti-AQP4 antibodies were positive (1:320), but no other paraneoplastic antibodies were identified. He was diagnosed with LM from lung adenocarcinoma causing secondary BVP via direct infiltration of the vestibulocochlear nerves. Dizziness improved with intrathecal chemotherapy. However, he died approximately one year after discharge. BVP may be the initial presentation of LM. It underscores the necessity of considering rare etiologies in patients with unexplained BVP. Early recognition and targeted therapy may improve neurological outcomes, although overall prognosis remains limited in the setting of disseminated malignancy.

title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics for preoperative prediction of tumor budding grade in rectal cancer.
abstract: Background Tumor budding (TB) is a histopathological marker of tumor aggressiveness and an established prognostic factor in colorectal cancer. In rectal cancer, however, TB is usually assessed on biopsy or resection material, and a reliable result may not be available when preoperative management is being considered. Purpose To develop and internally validate a radiomics model for preoperative discrimination of low-grade versus intermediate/high-grade TB in patients with rectal cancer who proceed to upfront surgery without neoadjuvant treatment. The primary model was selected according to the highest repeated cross-validation AUC, with alternative feature sets and algorithms evaluated exploratorily. Radiomics features were extracted from the tumor core, a combined tumor-plus-2-mm expansion, and an isolated external 2-mm ring. Seven feature sets and four machine-learning algorithms were evaluated; the primary model was selected according to the highest repeated cross-validation AUC. Feature filtering, imputation, selection, and scaling were performed within the training portion of every split. Model performance was estimated using stratified five-fold cross-validation repeated five times and patient-level out-of-fold (OOF) probabilities. Results The primary core-ROI Elastic Net model achieved a repeated cross-validation AUC of 0.825 (range 0.809-0.839 across repetitions), with PR-AUC 0.781, sensitivity 0.604, specificity 0.851, and Brier score 0.173. title: Clinical and radiological features of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome in children: a retrospective study.
abstract: Background Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is an uncommon but critical neurological emergency in children. Data on Chinese pediatric cohorts remain limited. Objective To analyze the clinical features, imaging findings, and treatment of PRES in children to improve early diagnosis and management. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 10 children diagnosed with PRES from March 2016 to January 2025. Results The patients included 7 males and 3 females, aged 3-13 years (mean 7.5 years). The main underlying diseases were acute lymphoblastic leukemia (3 cases) and nephrotic syndrome (3 cases). Eight children (80%) had hypertension, 6 (60%) had hypoalbuminemia, and 8 received glucocorticoids or immunosuppressants. The main symptoms were headache, seizures, impaired consciousness, and visual disturbances. Cranial MRI showed symmetrical long T1 and long T2 signals in bilateral posterior cerebral white matter. After comprehensive treatment including antihypertensive, anticonvulsant, and dehydration therapy, all symptoms resolved and lesions disappeared on follow-up imaging without sequelae. Conclusion Pediatric PRES is an acute reversible disorder associated with hypertension and immunosuppressive therapy. Early MRI diagnosis and prompt intervention can significantly improve prognosis.

title: An ultrasound-based nomogram for predicting early neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis.
abstract: To develop and validate an ultrasound-based nomogram prediction model for the early diagnosis of neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC). This is a retrospective cohort study. A total of 500 preterm infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) of our hospital from January 2023 to June 2024 were enrolled. They were stratified by NEC status and randomly assigned to a development cohort and a validation cohort at a ratio of 7:3. According to whether NEC occurred, infants were further categorized into an NEC group and a non-NEC group. General clinical data, including gestational age and birth weight, were collected. Laboratory inflammatory markers included C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and interleukin-6 (IL-6). Ultrasound parameters included bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, gastric antral area, gastric antral peristalsis, and bowel wall blood perfusion. Logistic regression analysis was performed in the development cohort to identify independent risk factors and construct a nomogram prediction model. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit in the development cohort. The validation cohort was used to verify model performance. Univariate analysis in the development cohort showed that gestational age, birth weight, CRP, PCT, IL-6, bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, gastric antral area, gastric antral peristalsis, and bowel wall blood perfusion differed significantly between groups (P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression further identified gestational age, CRP, PCT, IL-6, bowel wall thickness, intestinal peristalsis, bowel wall blood perfusion, gastric antral area, and gastric antral peristalsis as independent factors associated with early NEC (P < 0.05). On this basis, a nomogram prediction model was established. The areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) in the development and validation cohorts were 0.88 and 0.85, respectively, indicating good discriminative ability. The optimal risk cut-off of 0.18 was determined by Youden index solely from the development cohort. At this fixed threshold, sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV were 82.4%, 81.2%, 51.4%, and 95.0% for the development cohort; the corresponding performance in the validation cohort was 77.2%, 76.0%, 43.8%, and 92.4%. Goodness-of-fit testing of the calibration curves showed chi-square = 1.235 and P = 0.998 in the development cohort, and chi-square = 1.642 and P = 0.995 in the validation cohort, suggesting favorable agreement between predicted probabilities and observed risks. Decision curve analysis showed that when the risk threshold was greater than 0.05, the nomogram provided significant clinical net benefit. The nomogram prediction model constructed from inflammatory and multiparametric ultrasound indicators demonstrates favorable predictive performance for the early diagnosis of neonatal NEC. It may provide clinicians with a noninvasive and repeatable auxiliary diagnostic tool, facilitating early intervention for NEC and improving prognosis.

title: Liveborn trisomy 22: a case report.
abstract: Introduction : Trisomy 22 is identified in 2%-5% of spontaneous abortions across various populations, making it the second most common trisomy in spontaneous abortions. Liveborn patients with complete trisomy 22 are rare and present with variable clinical findings. Methods A detailed clinical report of a term female neonate with complete trisomy 22 was compiled after obtaining informed consent from her mother. Results The neonate was born via spontaneous vaginal delivery, and resuscitation included intubation after multiple attempts. She presented with multiple congenital anomalies, including a single umbilical artery, microcephaly, dysmorphic facial features, absent red reflex, corneal haze, irregular pupil, microcornea, imperforated anus with rectovestibular fistula, bilateral clinodactyly of the fifth digits, and bilateral distal and proximal transverse palmar creases running parallel to each other. An echocardiogram showed Tetralogy of Fallot and hypoplasia of the transverse aortic arch. Abdominal ultrasound revealed small kidneys. The electroencephalogram showed diffuse cerebral dysfunction. Head ultrasound indicated absence of the septum pellucidum. Additional complications included pneumothorax, metabolic disturbances, sepsis, and persistent thrombocytopenia. The neonate's condition deteriorated, leading to demise on the seventh day of life. Chromosome analysis confirmed 47,XX,+22. Discussion : This case report contributes to the limited literature on complete trisomy 22, highlighting its prognosis, clinical heterogeneity, and management challenges. The constellation of anomalies observed underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and adaptability in providing optimal care. By better understanding its clinical presentation, we hope to facilitate early recognition, appropriate management, and counseling.

title: CT habitat and peritumoral radiomics for predicting progression after repeat TACE in hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicenter study.
abstract: Background This study developed and validated an machine-learning-based radiomics model integrating tumor habitat radiomics, peritumoral radiomics, and clinical features to predict progression-free survival (PFS) following repeat transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 270 patients with HCC. Patients from Center 1 were assigned to training (n = 94) and internal validation (n = 41) cohorts, while Centers 2 (n = 82) and 3 (n = 53) served as external validation cohorts. Tumor habitats and 5-mm peritumoral regions were generated from contrast-enhanced CT images. Radiomics features were selected using univariate Cox and LASSO-Cox regression. A fusion model and HPC risk score were constructed by integrating selected radiomics signatures and clinical variables. Performance was assessed using time-dependent ROC, C-index, calibration, decision curve analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analyses. Results The optimal habitat cluster number was K = 2. Eleven habitat features, three peritumoral features, and alpha-fetoprotein were retained in the fusion model. The model achieved AUCs of 0.923, 0.921, and 0.897 for 3-, 6-, and 9-month progression-free survival in the training cohort, and 0.932, 0.863, and 0.916 in the internal validation cohort, respectively; all external AUCs exceeded 0.82. The fusion model showed higher C-index values than the clinical model across cohorts. High-risk patients had significantly shorter PFS than low-risk patients (all P < 0.001). Calibration and decision curve analyses demonstrated good agreement and clinical utility. Conclusion The CT-based fusion model and HPC risk score effectively predicted progression risk in HCC.

title: Functional assessment of experimental lymphedema: a focused mini-review of animal models and measurement methods.
abstract: Lymphedema is a chronic progressive disease resulting from impaired lymphatic transport. A wide range of animal models has been developed to study their pathophysiology, yet how well lymphatic function is measured within these models has received comparatively little attention. This mini-review organizes assessment methodologies into three complementary tiers: Tier 1 covers morphological and indirect outcome measures, including volumetric quantification and histological assessment; Tier 2 covers imaging-based approaches, including near-infrared fluorescence lymphangiography, radionuclide lymphoscintigraphy, and magnetic resonance lymphangiography; and Tier 3 covers direct physiological measurement of physical quantities such as intraluminal pressure, lymphatic conductance, and albumin transport rate. Surveying primary studies across seven species, we identify a recurring mismatch between the species most commonly used for lymphedema modeling and those in which the most informative measurements are technically accessible. The most accessible endpoints tend to reflect late-stage tissue consequences rather than early pumping dysfunction, imaging readouts remain constrained to relative dye intensity rather than true physical flow quantities, and direct physiological measurement is sparse and limited to single time points. For acquired secondary lymphedema, the rat hindlimb model paired with quantitative longitudinal imaging and vessel-level analysis offers a balanced platform, whereas genetic mouse models remain preferable for congenital disease and large-animal models for microsurgical and clinical-scale intervention studies; a cross-tabulation by species and measurement tier is provided to guide model and assessment selection.

title: CuFormer U-Net: a transformer-enhanced multi-task network for cucumber leaf disease detection and segmentation.
abstract: Cucumber foliar symptoms reduce functional leaf area and complicate greenhouse scouting. This study presents CuFormer U-Net, a Transformer-enhanced multi-task network for three-class image-level classification on the 3,754-image Kaggle benchmark (healthy, powdery mildew, and downy mildew) and binary visible-symptom segmentation on a separate 400-image greenhouse cohort (200 healthy and 200 affected leaves). The greenhouse annotations comprise 2,705 rectangles (1,741 color-abnormality and 964 tissue-damage instances); rectangle-seeded lesion masks were manually refined for the dense-prediction experiments. The reported fixed-split point estimates were 96.7% accuracy, 96.3% macro precision, 95.8% macro recall, and 96.0% macro F1 for classification, and 92.4% mean image-wise Dice, 83.1% macro IoU, 93.2% foreground precision, and 91.7% foreground recall for segmentation. The complete internal-validation ablation configuration reached 93.1% Dice and 87.3% IoU. The available experiment archive does not contain independent-seed reruns, per-image predictions for inferential testing, annotator-level masks, quantitative results for the separate 100-image greenhouse stress-test cohort, or reproducible hardware profiling. Accordingly, all between-model differences are interpreted descriptively, the external cohort is not presented as formal external validation, and robustness and deployment claims have been moderated. CuFormer U-Net provides a technically motivated basis for joint recognition and spatial characterization, but confirmatory multi-run and multi-site evaluation is required. boundary refinement, cucumber leaf disease, multi-task learning, plant disease, precision agriculture, semantic segmentation, vision transformer.
