title: Nutritional and Biochemical Correlates of Disease Severity and Hospitalization in Adults with Drug-resistant Tuberculosis: A Prospective Study from North India.
abstract: Background Drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) remains a major public health challenge in high-burden countries. While microbiological diagnosis is central to management, factors determining disease severity and hospitalization at presentation are less well characterized, particularly simple clinical and biochemical markers that may aid early risk stratification. Objectives To evaluate the clinical, nutritional, radiological, and biochemical profile of adults with confirmed DR-TB and to identify factors associated with disease severity, bacillary burden, and hospitalization. Methods This prospective observational study enrolled adults (>14 years) with confirmed DR-TB treated at a tertiary care DR-TB center in New Delhi between April and December 2022. Demographic, clinical, nutritional, biochemical, radiological, and microbiological data were collected at baseline. Disease severity was assessed using chest radiograph extent and sputum smear grading. Associations were analyzed using correlation and comparative statistical methods. Results A total of 55 patients were included (mean age: 26.6 ± 13.3 years), with a female predominance (52.7%). Undernutrition was common, with a mean body mass index of 17.3 ± 2.7 kg/m2 and 63.6% of patients underweight. Greater radiographic severity correlated with lower body mass index (BMI), higher symptom burden, and higher sputum smear grades (P < 0.01). Elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) levels were consistently associated with cough severity, dyspnea, radiographic extent, higher smear grades, and need for hospitalization. Lower serum protein and magnesium levels were associated with higher bacillary burden. Nearly half of the patients (47.3%) required hospitalization at diagnosis, which was significantly associated with lower BMI, hypoproteinemia, and elevated ALP levels. Conclusion In adults with DR-TB, disease severity and hospitalization at presentation are closely associated with nutritional depletion and biochemical derangements in addition to microbiological burden. Simple, routinely available parameters such as BMI, serum protein, ALP, and magnesium may help identify high-risk patients early and support triage and management decisions in resource-limited settings.

While microbiological diagnosis is central to management, factors determining disease severity and hospitalization at presentation are less well characterized, particularly simple clinical and biochemical markers that may aid early risk stratification.

To evaluate the clinical, nutritional, radiological, and biochemical profile of adults with confirmed DR-TB and to identify factors associated with disease severity, bacillary burden, and hospitalization.

This prospective observational study enrolled adults (>14 years) with confirmed DR-TB treated at a tertiary care DR-TB center in New Delhi between April and December 2022. A total of 55 patients were included (mean age: 26.6 ± 13.3 years), with a female predominance (52.7%). In adults with DR-TB, disease severity and hospitalization at presentation are closely associated with nutritional depletion and biochemical derangements in addition to microbiological burden. title: Validation of Baveno VII Criteria using Liver and Splenic Elastography for Predicting Esophageal Varices Severity in Chronic Liver Disease: A Multiparametric, Observational Study.
abstract: Background and aims Baveno VII criteria prioritize Liver Stiffness Measurement (LSM) for portal hypertension risk stratification, primarily using transient elastography. We aimed to evaluate two-dimensional-shear wave elastography (2D-SWE) cutoffs, assess the etiology-dependent utility of spleen stiffness (SSM), and introduce a novel Combined Hepato-splenic Stiffness Index (CHSSI). Materials and methods This ambispective, observational study enrolled 100 chronic liver disease patients. Participants underwent 2D-SWE for LSM and SSM, alongside endoscopy as the reference standard. A novel multiparametric index, CHSSI, was formulated. Diagnostic accuracy for Varices Needing Treatment (VNT; Grade >= II) was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC). Results The cohort was predominantly Alcohol-related Liver Disease (ALD, 49%) and Viral Hepatitis (30%). LSM independently predicted VNT (P < 0.001), with an optimal 2D-SWE cutoff of 19.2 kPa (sensitivity 90% and specificity 82%). SSM utility diverged by etiology: it correlated significantly with variceal grade in ALD (r = 0.549, P < 0.001) but poorly in viral cirrhosis (r = 0.174, P = 0.358). The novel CHSSI demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance (AUROC 0.892) for predicting VNT. Conclusions Liver stiffness remains the most robust single-parameter surrogate for esophageal varices. However, in heterogeneous cohorts where splenic stiffness alone yields inconsistent results, novel composite indices such as CHSSI and Liver Size-stiffness Index offer superior discriminative ability. These findings support a refined noninvasive risk stratification strategy, potentially reducing unnecessary screening endoscopies.

title: Impact of Triple Assessment on Surgical Decision-making in Thyroid Nodule Management.
abstract: Introduction Accurate preoperative assessment of thyroid nodules is crucial for distinguishing malignant from benign lesions and making optimal decisions. Triple assessment using clinical examination, ultrasonography (USG), and fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) has been increasingly used to improve diagnostic accuracy. Aim The aim of the study was to evaluate the efficacy of triple assessment in the detection and treatment of thyroid nodules by correlating ultrasonographic findings, clinical evaluation, and FNAC results with histopathological diagnosis. Methods This study was a prospective observational study of 56 patients with thyroid nodules undergoing surgical management. Data were collected prospectively using structured case record forms. Baseline information, physical examination findings, USG features, FNAC records, operative details, and histopathological reports were documented. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Frequency and percentage were used to present categorical variables. The diagnostic accuracy of clinical examination, USG, FNAC, and triple assessment was evaluated by estimating specificity, sensitivity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value, and diagnostic accuracy. Results A higher proportion of participants were female (85.7%) and were in the 41-60 years old age group. Histopathology confirmed benign lesions in 57.14% and malignant lesions in 42.86% of cases. Triple assessment achieved the most effective diagnostic accuracy, showing a sensitivity of 100%, a specificity of 87.50%, with a NPV of 100% and an overall diagnostic accuracy of 97.86%. Conclusion Triple assessment is a dependable and useful modality for assessing thyroid nodules. Combined use of clinical examination, USG, and FNAC reduces false-negative results and supports appropriate clinical decision-making.

title: Endodontic-Periodontal Lesions: Biological Basis, Diagnostic Challenges, and Contemporary Management Strategies.
abstract: Abstract The dental pulp and periodontium are intimately connected through anatomical structures such as the apical foramen, lateral and accessory canals, and dentinal tubules, creating pathways for the bidirectional spread of infection and inflammation. This close relationship can result in endodontic-periodontal lesions, which often present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to overlapping clinical and radiographic features. This review aims to examine the etiopathogenesis, classification, diagnostic considerations, and contemporary management approaches for endodontic-periodontal lesions. A narrative review of classical and current literature was conducted, focusing on the anatomical and biological interrelationship between pulpal and periodontal tissues, microbial interactions, disease progression, and evidence-based treatment protocols. The reviewed literature indicates that endodontic infections commonly produce secondary periodontal manifestations through the dissemination of microorganisms and their by-products along established anatomical pathways, while advanced periodontal disease may, under certain circumstances, adversely affect pulpal health. Accurate diagnosis requires a comprehensive assessment incorporating pulp vitality testing, periodontal examination, probing patterns, radiographic evaluation, and correlation of clinical findings. Successful treatment outcomes depend on correctly identifying the primary source of infection and implementing an appropriate treatment sequence. In most cases, endodontic therapy should be initiated before periodontal intervention to facilitate healing, permit reassessment of periodontal status, and guide the need for additional periodontal treatment. A thorough understanding of the endodontic-periodontal relationship remains essential for predictable diagnosis, treatment planning, and long-term prognosis.

title: Synchronous Leiomyomas of the Sigmoid Colon and Ileocecal Valve Presenting as Colonic Polyps in a Young Male.
abstract: Abstract Gastrointestinal (GI) leiomyomas are rare benign smooth muscle tumors, most commonly arising in the esophagus and stomach. Their occurrence in the colon is uncommon, and synchronous involvement of multiple colonic sites is exceedingly rare. We report a case of a young male who underwent colonoscopic evaluation for GI symptoms, which revealed polypoidal lesions in the sigmoid colon and at the ileocecal valve. Both lesions were endoscopically resected. Histopathology with immunohistochemistry is essential for accurate diagnosis and to differentiate these lesions from GI stromal tumors. Recognition of this entity is important to guide appropriate management and avoid overtreatment.

title: Biochemical-sonographic Correlations in First-trimester Screening for Foetal Aneuploidy: A Cross-sectional Study from Eastern India.
abstract: Background Aneuploidy screening constitutes an essential component of routine prenatal care worldwide, which is done by ultrasonography during the first trimester. Moreover, pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A) and free β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) reflect placental function, which serve as important biochemical markers for aneuploidy risk assessment. Aim The present study investigated the correlation between maternal serum PAPP-A and free β-hCG levels with first-trimester ultrasound screening markers, i.e. nuchal translucency (NT) thickness and nasal bone (NB) for detecting fetal aneuploidy. Materials and methods This was a cross-sectional observational study, which enrolled 139 women with singleton pregnancies at 11-14 weeks of gestation. First-trimester ultrasonography was performed by an experienced doctor, and maternal serum PAPP-A and free β-hCG were also measured. Correlation investigation was done by Spearman's correlation coefficient, while associations were done by Fisher's exact test. Results A significant positive correlation was observed between PAPP-A gestational age and maternal body mass index. Further, there were a strong negative correlation of NT thickness with PAPP-A multiples of the median (MoM) (P < 0.001) and a strong positive correlation with β-hCG MoM (P < 0.001). The fetal NB was absent in seven (5.0%) pregnancies, of which three were confirmed to have chromosomal abnormalities by noninvasive prenatal testing. Absent NB demonstrated 42.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity, while β-hCG levels were significantly higher in NB-negative pregnancies (P < 0.01). Conclusions The combined assessment of PAPP-A, free β-hCG, NT thickness, and fetal NB could improve the performance of first-trimester screening for fetal aneuploidy, enabling more accurate early prenatal risk stratification and facilitating timely clinical decision-making.

title: Breathing but Not Living: The Deceptive Stability of Hydranencephaly.
abstract: Abstract Hydranencephaly is a rare, fatal congenital brain malformation characterized by near-complete absence of cerebral hemispheres with preservation of posterior fossa structures. We report a male neonate born at 35 weeks with severe respiratory distress, profound hypotonia, and bulging anterior fontanelle. Transfontanellar ultrasound identified the pathognomonic "falx sign." Cranial computed tomography confirmed Type II hydranencephaly with complete bilateral hemispheric absence, preserved thalami and brainstem, and intact cerebellum. The infant required mechanical ventilation but was successfully extubated on day 5, demonstrating preserved brainstem function. However, this early stability does not alter the universal grave prognosis (median survival 5-6 months). This case emphasizes the importance of rapid neuroimaging in neonates presenting with hypotonia and respiratory distress, and the critical need for honest prognostic counseling and early palliative care involvement.

title: When Erectile Dysfunction Therapy Clouds the Vision: Central Serous Chorioretinopathy after Sildenafil in a Healthy Male.
abstract: Abstract Central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) is a pachychoroid-spectrum disorder characterized by serous neurosensory retinal detachment secondary to choroidal vascular congestion and retinal pigment epithelial dysfunction. While corticosteroid use and psychological stress are well-established risk factors, phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors such as sildenafil citrate, widely used for erectile dysfunction, have been increasingly recognized as an under-reported pharmacological trigger, with proposed mechanisms involving acute choroidal vasodilation and hyperpermeability. A 39-year-old previously healthy male presented with sudden, painless diminution of vision in the right eye of 48 h, occurring shortly after ingestion of a single large recreational dose of sildenafil citrate. Best-corrected visual acuity was reduced to 6/18 in the right eye, with a normal left eye. Fundus examination revealed a well-demarcated serous macular elevation, and optical coherence tomography (OCT) confirmed a dome-shaped neurosensory detachment with a markedly elevated central subfield thickness. A comprehensive systemic and hematological workup, including thrombophilia screening and cardiac evaluation, was unremarkable, supporting a diagnosis of sildenafil-induced CSCR. The patient was managed conservatively with topical nepafenac, topical Flurbiprofen, and oral alcaftadine, along with cessation of further sildenafil use. Serial follow-up over approximately 2 months demonstrated progressive resolution of subretinal fluid, normalization of central subfield thickness, and preservation of visual acuity, with OCT angiography confirming adequate perfusion and no neovascular complication. This case reinforces sildenafil as a potential, dose-related precipitant of acute CSCR even after a single high dose in patients without conventional risk factors. Prompt recognition, drug cessation, and conservative management resulted in complete anatomical and visual recovery, highlighting the importance of a thorough medication history in young patients presenting with unexplained central visual disturbance.

title: Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury with Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) Scoring Versus Renal Resistive Index (RRI) in Patients Undergoing On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background The diagnosis of acute kidney injury (AKI) using conventional markers such as serum creatinine and urine output is often delayed, prompting interest in bedside ultrasound-based predictors. This study compared renal resistive index (RRI) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) scoring for early prediction of AKI after on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Methods In this prospective observational study, 180 adult patients were enrolled. RRI and VExUS assessments were performed preoperatively and within 3 hours of cardiothoracic ICU admission. AKI was diagnosed within 48 hours postoperatively using kidney disease: improving global outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed for RRI and VExUS parameters, and diagnostic accuracy was assessed using area under ROC curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity. Results AKI occurred in 48 patients (26.7%). Postoperative RRI showed excellent discrimination for AKI (AUROC 0.854; cut-off ≥0.68: sensitivity 75%, specificity 86%, negative predictive value [NPV] 90.5%), outperforming preoperative RRI (AUROC 0.681). VExUS showed limited predictive performance (preoperative AUROC 0.588; postoperative AUROC 0.623). The baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in the AKI group was significantly lower than in the patients who did not develop AKI [70.3 ml/min/1.73 m2 vs 79.4 ml/min/1.73 m2]. Diabetes mellitus was more common in the AKI group (62.5% vs 35.6%, P = 0.002). Postoperative urine output remained significantly lower in AKI patients on day 1 and day 2 (P < 0.001). Conclusion Postoperative RRI ≥ 0.68 demonstrated the best predictive performance for early AKI in our cohort, outperforming preoperative RRI, ΔRRI or change in RRI, and VExUS scores, supporting the predominant role of intrarenal arterial hemodynamic alterations in early postoperative renal injury.

title: Ultrasound Measurement of Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter for Detection of Elevated Intracranial Pressure in Pediatric Encephalitis.
abstract: Background and objectives Elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) is a critical and potentially life-threatening complication of pediatric encephalitis. Early detection is essential for improved outcomes. This study assessed the diagnostic utility of optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) ultrasound for identifying elevated ICP in children with encephalitis. Methods A prospective descriptive case series was conducted at the Infectious Disease Intensive Care Unit (ID-ICU), Children's Hospital 1, Ho Chi Minh City, from August 2023 to April 2025. Children with encephalitis underwent daily ONSD ultrasound during the first seven days of admission. Elevated ICP was defined based on clinical signs and neuroimaging findings. ONSD measurements were compared between patients with and without elevated ICP, and age-specific diagnostic cut-off values were determined. Results Thirty-six patients were enrolled, with elevated ICP confirmed in 72.2% of cases. ONSD values were higher in patients with raised ICP than in those without at all time points. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis identified optimal ONSD thresholds for detecting elevated ICP of 5.2 mm in children younger than 60 months, 5.9 mm in those aged 60 months or older, and 5.6 mm in the overall cohort. Serial measurements showed a decline in ONSD over time. No significant difference was observed between right and left eye measurements, with strong inter-eye correlation. Conclusions Ultrasound measurement of ONSD is a useful, noninvasive, repeatable bedside tool for early identification of elevated ICP in pediatric encephalitis. Incorporating age-specific ROC-derived ONSD thresholds may improve diagnostic accuracy and support bedside assessment in pediatric intensive care settings.

title: Preoperative apical margin risk estimation from T2-weighted MRI radiomics in prostate cancer with MRI-visible apical tumors: toward multidisciplinary decision support.
abstract: This retrospective study developed and validated a T2-weighted imaging (T2WI)-based radiomics model for preoperative prediction of apical positive surgical margins (PSMs) in patients undergoing radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer. Overall, 235 patients (74 with apical PSMs and 161 without apical PSMs) were randomly divided into a training set (n = 164; 69.8%) and an independent test set (n = 71; 30.2%). Eligible patients had preoperative multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging within 6 weeks before surgery, an index lesion involving or abutting the prostatic apex, definitive apical margin status, and standard radical prostatectomy without nerve-sparing. Patients with inadequate imaging for apical assessment or region-of-interest delineation, prior transurethral resection of the prostate, or neoadjuvant androgen-deprivation therapy were excluded. A total of 1409 radiomic features were extracted from T2WI. After normalization and removal of highly correlated features (|r| > 0.99), six optimal features were selected by recursive feature elimination. A gradient boosting machine model was constructed, and performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier score, and decision curve analysis. The apical PSM rate was 31.5%. In the test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.874, Brier score of 0.120, accuracy of 87.3%, sensitivity of 81.8%, and specificity of 89.8%. Skewness was the most important feature, contributing 34.8% to the model. Apical PSMs were significantly associated with extraprostatic extension (P = 0.001), and the tumor-margin model provided the greatest net clinical benefit. T2WI-based radiomics may support individualized preoperative risk assessment and surgical planning for prostate cancer.

title: Triglyceride-Glucose Index and Incident Stroke in Elderly Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been associated with stroke in general populations. However, evidence regarding its prognostic value for incident stroke in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains limited. Objectives To evaluate the association between the TyG index and incident stroke in elderly patients with T2DM. A retrospective cohort study conducted at a provincial tertiary care center in Northern Thailand. Materials and methods This study included 1024 patients aged ≥60 years with T2DM. The TyG index was calculated from fasting triglyceride and fasting plasma glucose levels at baseline and categorized into quartiles. The primary outcome was computed tomography-confirmed incident stroke during a 5-year follow-up. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for age, sex, hypertension, and smoking status. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression. Results Over a mean follow-up of 4.7 years, 51 patients (5.0%) developed incident stroke. Although higher TyG index quartiles were associated with less favorable metabolic profiles, no significant differences in stroke-free survival were observed across TyG quartiles. In multivariable analyses, the TyG index was not independently associated with incident stroke, whether analyzed as quartiles or as a continuous variable. Conclusions The TyG index was not associated with incident stroke in elderly patients with T2DM, suggesting limited prognostic utility of the TyG index for stroke risk prediction in this population.

title: Deep Learning-based Regression of Intraoperative Estimated Blood Loss from Preoperative Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Patients Undergoing Intracranial Meningioma Surgery.
abstract: Background Preoperative estimation of intraoperative blood loss remains challenging in patients undergoing meningioma surgery. Deep learning (DL) provides a potential imaging-based approach for personalized blood loss prediction without handcrafted feature engineering. Objectives The primary objective was to develop a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based regression model that can predict continuous intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) during intracranial meningioma surgery from the preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images. In addition, the secondary objective was to compare the regression performance of the CNN model with a baseline regression model. Materials and methods This was a retrospective study of 632 patients with intracranial meningioma who had undergone surgery with prior MRI. The patients were patient-wise split into training (n = 442), validation (n = 126), and independent test (n = 64) cohorts. A CNN model was trained to forecast the continuous EBL based on multiparametric MRI images. In the model evaluation, image-level predictions from each patient were averaged together to get a single patient-level prediction. The coefficient of determination (R2), mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), Bland-Altman analysis, and bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were used to evaluate model performance. A training-mean baseline model was used as a comparison. Results The proposed CNN achieved moderate patient-level predictive performance with an R2 of 0.631 (95% CI, 0.479, 0.697), MAE of 382.1 mL (95% CI, 316.7, 452.1), RMSE of 466.6 mL (95% CI, 395.2, 536.0), and MAPE of 75.8% (95% CI, 49.4, 110.4). The CNN lowered the MAE by 37.2%, the RMSE by 39.8%, and the MAPE by 30.7%, when compared to the baseline at the training mean. Median aggregation yielded similar performance, suggesting that patient-level predictive performance was not materially sensitive to the choice of mean versus median aggregation in the test cohort. Conclusions Patient-level regression performance of the CNN model demonstrated moderate internal predictive performance, but its clinical utility and the imaging features underlying its predictions remain uncertain. Future studies should focus on external validation and multimodal integration to improve the predictive performance and clinical applicability.

title: Ultrasound-derived mean grayscale intensity for predicting malignant pleural effusion: A prospective study.
abstract: Background Early recognition of malignant pleural effusion is important for prognosis and treatment planning. Quantitative, noninvasive imaging parameters may aid in diagnosing pleural malignancy. This study investigated the diagnostic value of mean grayscale intensity (MGI) measurements obtained from thoracic ultrasound images for differentiating benign and malignant pleural effusions. Methods In this prospective observational study, 101 patients with pleural effusion were enrolled. MGI measurements were performed on stored thoracic ultrasound images using ImageJ software. Patients were classified as having benign or malignant pleural effusion based on cytological and/or histopathological findings or, in patients without pathological confirmation, two negative pleural fluid cytology examinations, the absence of additional clinical or radiological findings suggestive of malignancy, and regression of the pleural effusion during follow-up. Independent predictors of malignant pleural effusion were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression analysis, and diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results Among the 101 patients, 59 had benign pleural effusion and 42 had malignant pleural effusion. The median MGI was significantly higher in malignant than in benign pleural effusions (21 vs. 18, P = 0.03). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, MGI remained independently associated with malignant pleural effusion (odds ratio: 1.052, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.003-1.103; P = 0.03). ROC analysis yielded an area under the curve of 0.62 (95% CI: 0.513-0.734). The optimal cutoff value was 24.25, with a sensitivity of 40.48% and a specificity of 79.66%. Conclusion MGI values obtained from thoracic ultrasound images were significantly higher in malignant pleural effusions and remained independently associated with pleural malignancy. Although MGI should not be considered a standalone diagnostic tool, it may serve as a quantitative, noninvasive imaging parameter that complements clinical, radiological, and ultrasonographic assessment.

title: Use of Dermoscopy in Prognostication and Therapeutic Monitoring of Non-neoplastic Disorders.
abstract: Abstract Dermoscopy has transformed from a toolprimarily used for assessing melanocytic and non-melanocytic skin tumors into an essential aid in general dermatology. Its application now extends to various ailments, such as infiltrative, pigmentary, inflammatory, and infectious dermatoses. Beyond facilitating early and accurate diagnosis, dermoscopy has gained recognition for its role in evaluating progression of disease and response to treatment. As a non-invasive imaging modality, it offers a significant advantage over histopathology, particularly in long-term disease monitoring. Recent studies highlight its ability to detect subtle changes indicative of therapeutic efficacy, allowing for timely modifications in management. By integrating dermoscopic evaluation into routine clinical practice, dermatologists can enhance diagnostic precision, predict disease prognosis, and refine treatment approaches, ultimately improving patient outcomes. This review explores the growing relevance of dermoscopy in non-neoplastic dermatoses, emphasizing its value in prognostic assessment and therapeutic monitoring.

title: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease misdiagnosed as angle closure: Demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, and visual outcomes.
abstract: Purpose To describe the clinical presentation, diagnostic delay, management, and visual outcomes of Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada (VKH) disease presenting initially as angle closure. Methods This retrospective study reviewed the medical records of patients diagnosed with VKH who initially presented with angle closure between January 2013 and December 2020. Clinical features, intraocular pressure (IOP), imaging, treatment modalities, and final visual outcomes were analyzed. Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed to identify factors influencing final BCVA (best corrected visual acuity). Results Among 768 VKH patients, 18 patients (36 eyes; 3.94%) presented with angle closure with a mean age of 44.4 years and a female preponderance (89%). Eighteen eyes had primary angle closure (PAC), and 18 eyes had secondary angle closure glaucoma (SACG) at presentation. The mean IOP at final follow-up decreased from 26.3 to 14 mmHg. Fundus evaluation was deferred in many due to media opacities, leading to delayed VKH diagnosis (median delay: 1 month to 7 years). Ancillary imaging revealed choroidal thickening and ciliochoroidal effusion in four eyes. Poorer presenting BCVA and delayed diagnosis (>1 month) were associated with worse final BCVA ( P = 0.011 and P = 0.0066, respectively) in univariate analysis, while presenting BCVA remained a statistically significant independent predictor of final visual outcome (p 0.039) in multivariate analysis. Conclusion VKH can uncommonly present as angle closure, often mimicking PAC or SACG. Early clinical suspicion, use of posterior segment imaging (optical coherence tomography, B-scan, ultrasound biomicroscopy), and prompt immunosuppressive therapy are essential for optimal management.

title: Long-term outcomes of vital pulp therapy in teeth affected by dental caries or trauma: A systematic review.
abstract: Background The utilization of vital pulp therapy (VPT) has significantly increased in immature and mature permanent teeth due to the advancement in calcium silicate-based biomaterials like Mineral Trioxide Aggregate (MTA), Biodentine, and other modern bioceramic formulations. However, long-term longevity and available evidence for treatment outcomes in different clinical conditions are still in a heterogeneous form. The study aimed to systematically assess the longevity, clinical success, and prognostic factors associated with VPT in teeth affected by Dental caries or traumatic pulp exposure. Materials and methods This systematic review was done by following the predetermined and structured screening process. The 1042 records were identified from Database searching. After removal of duplicate records and after eligibility assessment, a total of 13 studies were included in the study for final analysis. The narrative synthesis of available evidence was done based on VPT technique, used biomaterial, tooth maturity, follow-up duration, and predictors associated with treatment success or failure. Results VPT has consistently shown the favorable clinical and radiographic outcomes in included studies. The reported success rates for Partial pulpotomy were 70% to 93%, while for complete/full pulpotomy it was 80% to 95%. The treatment success for mature permanent teeth was 70% to 100%, whereas more consistent treatment outcomes were observed in immature permanent teeth, in which success rates were 84.5% to 93.1%. The continued root development and apexogenesis were frequently reported. Bioceramic materials have shown significant favorable results than calcium hydroxide. 85% success rate was reported for MTA after 24 months in one randomized clinical trial, whereas it was 43% for calcium hydroxide. Biodentine has shown the favorable outcomes as like MTA, whereas new fast-setting calcium silicate cements have shown more than 90% success rates in selected studies. The treatment outcomes during short-term and medium-term follow-up had remained favorable with 85%-90% success after 24 months in many studies. Conclusion The current evidence suggests that the VPT predictable and durable treatment method for teeth affected by carious or traumatic pulp exposures. Especially, the calcium silicate-based biomaterials like MTA and Biodentine have shown the high clinical success in different clinical conditions. The pulp vitality can be successfully preserved in immature and mature permanent teeth by using adequate biomaterials, restorative strategies, and case-selection criteria.

title: Design of a novel dental bone mapping caliper for chairside ridge assessment: A technical note.
abstract: Background Accurate assessment of alveolar ridge width is essential for implant treatment planning. Although cone-beam computed tomography provides detailed three-dimensional information, chairside ridge-mapping techniques remain valuable because of their simplicity, accessibility, and cost-effectiveness. Objective The objective of this study was to describe the design, clinical application, and potential advantages of a novel dental bone mapping caliper for transgingival ridge assessment. Technical description The proposed instrument incorporates a blunt external reference arm, a controlled transgingival probing tip, a calibrated sliding measurement scale, and an ergonomically designed handle within a single device. The instrument enables direct chairside measurement of alveolar ridge width while improving stabilization and measurement standardization. Clinical application The caliper is used during transgingival ridge mapping by positioning the blunt arm against the mucosal surface and advancing the probing tip until cortical bone contact is achieved. Measurements are recorded directly from the calibrated scale. Discussion Compared with conventional ridge-mapping methods, the proposed design offers improved operator control, direct measurement recording, enhanced stability, and simplified clinical workflow. However, clinical validation studies are required to determine its accuracy, reproducibility, and patient acceptance. Conclusion The novel dental bone mapping caliper represents a practical chairside tool for ridge assessment and may improve the standardization of transgingival bone mapping procedures. Further clinical investigations are necessary to establish its effectiveness relative to existing methods.

title: Completion cholecystectomy for remnant gall bladder stones: A tertiary centre experience.
abstract: Introduction Remnant gall bladder and cystic duct stump calculi are uncommon but significant causes of post-cholecystectomy syndrome, often presenting after a prolonged interval and posing diagnostic and technical challenges. Evidence from contemporary Indian cohorts remains limited and heterogeneous. Patients and methods This retrospective observational study analysed 22 consecutive patients who underwent completion cholecystectomy for symptomatic remnant gall bladder or cystic duct stump calculi between January 2015 and December 2024 at a tertiary referral centre. Patients with radiologically confirmed remnant pathology and prior sub-total or difficult cholecystectomy were included. Clinical, imaging, operative, perioperative and follow-up outcomes were analysed. Results The mean age was 47.8 years with female predominance (77.2%). The median interval between index surgery and symptom onset was 4 years. Biliary colic was the most common presentation (86.4%), with complications in 18.2% of patients. Ultrasonography detected pathology in 76%, whereas magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) demonstrated 100% diagnostic accuracy. Laparoscopic completion cholecystectomy was successfully performed in 86.4% of patients, with a conversion rate of 9%. The mean operative duration was 118 min, and the mean blood loss was 87 ml. Critical view of safety was achieved in 50% of cases. Post-operative complications (Clavien-Dindo >II) occurred in 13.6% of patients, with no mortality. The median hospital stay was 2 days. At a median follow-up of 26 months, all patients achieved complete relief of biliary pain, although 35% of patients reported mild dyspeptic symptoms. Conclusions Completion cholecystectomy is a safe and effective definitive treatment for remnant gall bladder and cystic duct stump calculi, with high laparoscopic feasibility and favourable outcomes in experienced hands. MRCP plays a crucial role in diagnosis and operative planning, while redo surgery remains technically demanding due to altered anatomy.

title: Comparison of Different Models in Calculation of Tumor Control Probability and Normal Tissue Complication Probability in Breast Cancer Radiotherapy.
abstract: The aim of this study is to compare tumor control probability (TCP) for the planning target volume (PTV) using Poisson, Niemierko, and Zaider-Minerbo models, and normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) for organs at risk (OARs) using Niemierko, Lyman-Kutcher-Burman (LKB) and relative seriality (RS) models. Radiotherapy dosimetry data of sixty breast cancer patients were utilized to calculate TCP and NTCP with various models. Patients underwent planning using a 16-slice CT scanner, delivering 50 Gy in 25 fractions using 6 MV photon beam energy and the Monaco treatment planning system (TPS). Significant differences in TCP were found between Poisson and Zaider-Minerbo models, and between Zaider-Minerbo and equivalent uniform dose (EUD) based models, with no difference between Poisson and EUD-based models. For NTCP, differences were observed between RS model and LKB for heart, spinal cord, and thyroid, as well as between RS model and EUD-based model for the heart, spinal cord and thyroid. LKB and EUD-based models showed differences when considering the lungs as an additional OAR. Differences among models for calculation TCP and NTCP emphasize the importance of considering specific treatment objectives and patient characteristics in breast cancer radiotherapy planning, ensuring optimized therapeutic outcomes while minimizing adverse effects on healthy tissues.

title: Role of early lung ultrasound in predicting disease progression of acute bronchiolitis.
abstract: Background Although clinical assessment is typically diagnostic for bronchiolitis in children, recent literature suggests that early lung ultrasound (LUS) can predict disease progression and help identify children at risk of developing severe illness. This is due to its non-invasive nature, safety, and ability to provide real-time, rapid findings. Purpose The aim of the study was to determine the correlation between early LUS findings and clinical severity scores. Additionally, the study sought to evaluate the role of early LUS in predicting disease progression and the severity of bronchiolitis, specifically in relation to the need for oxygen supplementation, the duration of oxygen therapy, the length of hospitalization, and intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Methods This was a single-centre prospective observational study conducted at a tertiary hospital in South India. Infants with mild-to-moderate bronchiolitis, as determined by clinical severity scores, underwent early LUS within the first 24 hours of their presentation to the hospital. They were categorized into mild, moderate, and severe groups based on bronchiolitis-specific early LUS findings. Daily clinical scores were recorded, and the highest clinical score was used to assess disease progression correlation. Results A total of 127 children, with a mean age of 5.02 ± 3 months, were recruited for the study. According to the modified TAL clinical bronchiolitis severity score, 71 children were classified as having mild bronchiolitis, while 56 had moderate bronchiolitis. The final analysis revealed that the early LUS score had a strong correlation with disease progression (rho = 0.869, P < 0.001). Additionally, the early LUS score significantly correlated with the need for supplemental oxygen (rho = 0.889, P < 0.001), length of hospital stay (rho = 0.851, P < 0.001), and ICU stay (rho = 0.904, P < 0.001). Conclusion Early LUS demonstrated a strong correlation with disease progression, as indicated by highest clinical scores in mild-to-moderate bronchiolitis.

title: Evaluation of Pharyngeal Airway Volume in Patients with Impacted Maxillary Canines Using Cone-beam Computed Tomography and Comparative Analysis of Artificial Intelligence-Based Segmentation Methods.
abstract: Background Impacted maxillary canines may be associated with alterations in adjacent craniofacial structures; however, their relationship with pharyngeal airway dimensions has not been directly investigated. Aim The aim of this study was to compare pharyngeal airway volume between individuals with impacted maxillary canines and a control group, and to evaluate the measurement outcomes obtained using semi-automatic and artificial intelligence (AI)-based segmentation methods. Methods Cone-beam computed tomography data from 120 retrospectively selected individuals were analyzed. Pharyngeal airway volumes were measured using a semi-automatic method (NemoFAB), and comparisons were made between the impacted canine group ( n = 70) and the control group ( n = 50). In the second phase, NemoFAB measurements from 95 patients were compared with those obtained from four different AI-based software programs. Non-parametric tests, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), and correlation analyses were performed for statistical evaluation. Results Airway volume, minimum cross-sectional area, and axial slice area values were significantly higher in the control group compared with the impacted canine group ( P ≤ 0.005). The group effect remained statistically significant after controlling for age and sex ( P < 0.001). Although statistically significant differences were observed between the AI-based programs and the semi-automatic method, high correlation coefficients ( r = 0.903-0.947) and strong intraclass correlation coefficient values indicated a high level of agreement between the methods. Conclusions The presence of impacted maxillary canines is associated with a reduction in pharyngeal airway volume. AI-based segmentation methods demonstrate a high level of agreement with the semi-automatic method and appear to be suitable for clinical and research applications.

title: Incidental Mandibular Intraosseous Findings in Neurofibromatosis Type 1: CBCT and MRI Features Influencing Clinical Management.
abstract: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) may involve the jaws without clinical symptoms and may affect orthodontic treatment planning. A 13-year-old female with NF1, diagnosed in childhood, was referred for orthodontic evaluation because of maxillary anterior crowding and Class III malocclusion. Routine panoramic radiography revealed incidental mandibular radiolucencies. Cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated multiple non-expansile intraosseous radiolucent findings in the anterior and posterior mandible, including a lesion close to an adjacent tooth root with mild buccal cortical thinning but no root resorption. Magnetic resonance imaging identified an intramedullary lesion in the right parasymphyseal region. As histopathological confirmation was not obtained, the exact nature of the findings remained uncertain. Following multidisciplinary consultation, mandibular orthodontic tooth movement and extractions were avoided as an individualized precautionary decision. Treatment was limited to skeletal anchorage-assisted maxillary expansion with facemask therapy, followed by fixed appliances in the maxillary arch. Follow-up imaging showed no aggressive changes and partial development of sclerotic changes. This case illustrates how clinically silent mandibular findings in NF1 may influence orthodontic treatment planning and supports individualized management based on multidisciplinary assessment and radiological surveillance.

title: Facial Balamuthia mandrillaris Infection.
abstract: This case report describes a rare cutaneous facial infection caused by Balamuthia mandrillaris. A 5-year-old boy presented with a red plaque on his left cheek lasting 14 months that had been previously misdiagnosed as a fungal infection without response to treatment. Routine fungal microscopy, histopathology, and molecular testing failed to identify the pathogen. Ultimately, next-generation sequencing of the skin lesion detected sequences of B. mandrillaris, which was subsequently confirmed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction testing. Examination of head magnetic resonance imaging confirmed no central nervous system involvement. The patient was treated with a combination regimen including lincomycin, sulfamethoxazole, and albendazole. After 3 months of therapy, the skin lesions subsided significantly, resulting in a favorable prognosis without the development of fatal granulomatous amebic encephalitis.

title: Computed Tomographic Features Associated with Pulmonary Melioidosis versus Pulmonary Tuberculosis in Diabetic Patients: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
abstract: Pulmonary melioidosis is frequently mistaken for pulmonary tuberculosis because of overlapping clinical and radiological features, often delaying appropriate treatment. We conducted a retrospective comparative cohort study at a tertiary care center in southern India between January 2018 and August 2025 to compare chest computed tomography (CT) features of microbiologically confirmed melioidosis and tuberculosis in diabetic adults who underwent CT within 30 days of symptom onset. A total of 151 patients were included: 46 with melioidosis and 105 with tuberculosis. Cavitation (n = 81/105 [77.1%] versus n = 20/46 [43.5%], P <0.001) and hydropneumothorax (n = 11/105 [10.5%] versus n = 0/46 [0%], P = 0.019) were more common in tuberculosis. In contrast, when compared with tuberculosis, melioidosis was associated with more frequent bilateral lung involvement (n = 37/105 [35.2%] versus n = 26/46 [56.5%], P = 0.015), pleural effusion (n = 28/105 [26.7%] versus n = 23/46 [50.0%], P = 0.005), and hilar lymphadenopathy (n = 6/105 [5.7%] versus n = 8/46 [17.4%], P = 0.032). Despite these differences, there was substantial overlap in CT findings, with upper-lobe predominance, centrilobular nodules, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy seen in both groups. In multivariable analysis, cavitation was associated with significantly lower odds of melioidosis than tuberculosis (adjusted odds ratio: 0.25, 95% CI: 0.12-0.54, P <0.001). Pulmonary melioidosis and pulmonary tuberculosis, therefore, show substantial overlap on chest CT in diabetic patients, and imaging should be interpreted as an adjunct to targeted microbiological diagnosis rather than a substitute for it.

title: Computed tomography angiography of congenital left-sided obstructive heart lesions: a pictorial essay.
abstract: Congenital left-sided obstructive heart lesions (LSOLs) are a group of rare but serious congenital heart diseases. They encompass a spectrum of structural abnormalities that can obstruct blood flow at any point from the left atrium to the aortic arch. They are broadly divided into two main categories. The first is left ventricular inflow obstruction, including cor triatriatum sinister and congenital mitral stenosis. The second is left ventricular outflow obstruction, including subvalvular aortic stenosis, bicuspid aortic valve, supravalvular aortic stenosis, coarctation of the aorta, aortic arch hypoplasia, and interrupted aortic arch. When stenosis involves both left ventricular inflow and outflow obstructions, the condition is called Shone's syndrome. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) is a valuable tool for the diagnosis, treatment planning, and follow-up of LSOLs. Our goal is to review the CTA manifestations of LSOLs to better understand these congenital heart lesions.

title: Ultrasound-guided coaxial aspiration for retrieval and repositioning of breast localization markers.
abstract: Breast localization marker migration or malposition may create a practical need for image-guided retrieval or repositioning. The technique was performed in two patients using a coaxial needle system and aspiration-assisted marker capture. In both cases, the displaced marker was identified sonographically and accessed with a coaxial needle. Controlled aspiration drew the marker into the coaxial needle, followed by repositioning to the targeted area or removal from the body. No immediate complications occurred. Ultrasound-guided coaxial aspiration may represent an alternative in selected cases of migrated or malpositioned markers when standard vacuum-assisted excision is technically disadvantageous.

title: Dual-energy computed tomography pulmonary angiography for pulmonary embolism: a three-tier evidence framework to guide individualized low-iodine scanning.
abstract: Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is widely studied for pulmonary embolism (PE) evaluation, but heterogeneity in protocols, platforms, and study designs complicates its clinical positioning. This narrative review, with structured search elements adapted from the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, synthesized evidence from PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (January 2016-June 2026); 28 studies were eligible (26 of 1,287 screened records and 2 identified through citation tracing). Evidence was organized into a three-tier framework (image quality, diagnostic performance, and clinical outcomes). Low-keV virtual monoenergetic imaging at 40-50 keV improves vascular attenuation and enables iodine load reduction to approximately 6 g in selected protocols. Pooled meta-analytic evidence shows no consistent diagnostic advantage of DECT over single-energy CT. The right ventricular/left ventricular diameter ratio remains the most stable prognostic indicator; DECT perfusion metrics have not surpassed it for mortality prediction. Iodine-map hypoperfusion in distal arteries is suspicious for, but not morphologically confirmed as, subsegmental PE; such findings carry a risk of overdiagnosis and warrant caution before anticoagulation. A body mass index- and estimated glomerular filtration rate-stratified protocol table with Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine 2011 evidence-level annotations is provided, and knowledge gaps in photon-counting CT, artificial intelligence, and cross-platform standardization are identified.

title: Automated measurement of calcaneal inclination angle via partial semantic segmentation using U-Net.
abstract: Purpose To develop and validate an interpretable deep learning pipeline for the automated measurement of the calcaneal inclination angle (CIA) on lateral weight-bearing foot radiographs using partial semantic segmentation. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 884 radiographs after the removal of duplicates, partitioned into a development cohort of 779 radiographs and a held-out internal test cohort of 105 radiographs, with no patient contributing to both. Three landmark-relevant anatomical regions were manually annotated: the inferior calcaneal contour (CAL), inferior contour of the fifth metatarsal head (M5), and calcaneal aspect of the inferior calcaneocuboid joint (CC). Each region was segmented by its own single-class U-Net model, trained from scratch with an unweighted Dice + Binary Cross-Entropy loss and early stopping on the validation Dice score, and deterministic post-processing was used to derive four anatomical landmarks and to calculate the CIA. A second observer, a fifth-year radiology resident, independently re-annotated a random subset of 50 development radiographs from a blank canvas. The train/validation split was performed at the patient level, and each network was trained with five predefined seeds. Segmentation performance was evaluated on the validation set, and clinical measurement accuracy was assessed on the held-out test set against three readers who measured independently and blinded. The frozen primary model was then applied without modification to an independent external cohort of 50 radiographs from a second institution, measured by the same three readers under the identical blinded protocol. Results Validation Dice scores across the five seeded training runs were 0.935 ± 0.010 for CAL, 0.871 ± 0.005 for M5, and 0.805 ± 0.009 for CC (mean ± standard deviation), with the pre-specified primary run reaching 0.936, 0.865, and 0.807, respectively. In the held-out test cohort, the model showed a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.690° (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.525-0.855) against the mean of the three readers, with 92.4% of measurements within 2° and 98.1% within 3°. Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a small negative bias of -0.425° (95% confidence interval -0.620° to -0.230°), with 95% limits of agreement from -2.427° to +1.577°. The intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) formula ICC(A,1) achieved 0.986 across the model and the three readers and 0.994 among the three readers alone. In the external cohort, the model achieved an MAE of 0.85° against the three-reader mean, with 92.0% of measurements within 2° and an ICC of 0.969. Conclusion Partial semantic segmentation combined with deterministic landmark extraction enables rapid and clinically accurate automated CIA measurement on lateral weight-bearing foot radiographs, with an agreement approaching, though not yet equaling, that observed among human readers. Clinical significance The proposed pipeline enabled fast, reproducible CIA measurement with high expert agreement and may support standardized foot alignment assessment after prospective validation.

The frozen primary model was then applied without modification to an independent external cohort of 50 radiographs from a second institution, measured by the same three readers under the identical blinded protocol.

Results

Validation Dice scores across the five seeded training runs were 0.935 ± 0.010 for CAL, 0.871 ± 0.005 for M5, and 0.805 ± 0.009 for CC (mean ± standard deviation), with the pre-specified primary run reaching 0.936, 0.865, and 0.807, respectively. In the held-out test cohort, the model showed a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.690° (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.525-0.855) against the mean of the three readers, with 92.4% of measurements within 2° and 98.1% within 3°. Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a small negative bias of -0.425° (95% confidence interval -0.620° to -0.230°), with 95% limits of agreement from -2.427° to +1.577°. The intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) formula ICC(A,1) achieved 0.986 across the model and the three readers and 0.994 among the three readers alone. In the external cohort, the model achieved an MAE of 0.85° against the three-reader mean, with 92.0% of measurements within 2° and an ICC of 0.969.

Conclusion

Partial semantic segmentation combined with deterministic landmark extraction enables rapid and clinically accurate automated CIA measurement on lateral weight-bearing foot radiographs, with an agreement approaching, though not yet equaling, that observed among human readers.

Clinical significance

The proposed pipeline enabled fast, reproducible CIA measurement with high expert agreement and may support standardized foot alignment assessment after prospective validation.

title: Association of 18 F-FDG PET/CT Radiomics with Tumor Molecular Features in Breast Cancer.
abstract: Objectives This study aims to investigate the potential relationship between radiomic features extracted from 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose ( 18 F-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) images of patients with breast cancer and molecular markers including estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER-2) and Ki-67. Methods Radiomic features were obtained via an open-source software (LIFEx) from 18 F-FDG PET/CT images of 162 patients with histopathologically confirmed breast cancer. In order to examine the association between each molecular marker and radiomic features, machine learning models were developed seperately using the Python software. After the data were divided into test and training subsets, features were selected and scaled. Using the selected features, five different machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression and Naive Bayes) were established and their performance was evaluated based on accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, balanced accuracy, MCC and area under the curve (AUC) the receiver operating characteristic curve. Results For HER-2 status, the model yielded an AUC of 0.76, a balanced accuracy of 0.76, a sensitivity of 62.5% and a specificity of 90.0%. For ER, PR and Ki-67 status, AUC values were 0.59, 0.55, 0.60, balanced accuracies were 0.65, 0.61, 0.62, sensitivities were 96.6%, 81.8%, 68.4% and specificities were 33.3%, 40.0%, 55.2% respectively. Conclusion In this study, radiomic features derived from 18 F-FDG PET/CT images demonstrated poor or non-discriminatory performance in the assessment of ER, PR and Ki-67 status. Although a preliminary signal of an association was observed for HER-2 status, this finding should be considered hypothesis-generating only due to the low number of HER-2-positive cases in the test subset and the lack of independent external validation. In larger cohorts prospective, multicenter studies are needed to validate this potential association.

title: Atypical Skull Base Metastasis from Pediatric Extremity Chondroblastic Osteosarcoma Detected by Surveillance 18 F-FDG PET/CT: A Case Report with Focused Literature Review.
abstract: A 15-year-old girl who had previously undergone surgery and chemotherapy for non-metastatic chondroblastic osteosarcoma of the left fibula was evaluated with 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ( 18 F-FDG PET/CT) during routine follow-up while in clinical remission. Imaging demonstrated a 36 × 17 mm hypermetabolic lesion in the right occipital condyle maximum standard uptake value [(SUV max ): 16.5], with adjacent bone and soft-tissue extension, together with a concurrent 18 F-FDG-avid pulmonary nodule (SUV max : 3.4). Shortly after imaging, the patient developed mild neck discomfort and right-sided tongue deviation, suggesting hypoglossal nerve involvement. Biopsy of the skull base lesion and histopathological evaluation of the pulmonary nodule confirmed metastatic chondroblastic osteosarcoma with concordant morphology and immunophenotype. The patient underwent biopsy of the occipital lesion, surgical excision, radiotherapy, and wedge resection of the pulmonary metastasis. Skull base involvement from osteosarcoma arising in the extremities is exceptional and is particularly rare in pediatric patients. This case highlights the complementary role of whole-body 18 F-FDG PET/CT in detecting atypical metastatic sites that may not be routinely assessed by conventional surveillance strategies. In addition, the focused literature review underscores the exceptional rarity of skull base involvement in pediatric chondroblastic osteosarcoma and supports the need for heightened awareness of uncommon metastatic patterns.

title: Prognostic Value of Primary Tumor and Immune Organ Metabolic Parameters Derived from Pretreatment 18 F-FDG PET/CT in Gastric Adenocarcinoma: A Retrospective Survival Analysis.
abstract: Objective To investigate the association of primary tumor volume-based parameters and immune organ (liver, spleen, bone marrow) metabolic parameters and their derived ratios [spleen-to-liver ratio (SLR), bone marrow-to-liver ratio (BLR), spleen-to-bone marrow ratio (SBR)], measured on pretreatment 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ( 18 F-FDG PET/CT), with overall survival in gastric adenocarcinoma. Methods 127 patients with histopathologically confirmed gastric adenocarcinoma who underwent pretreatment 18 F-FDG PET/CT were retrospectively evaluated. Maximum standardized uptake value, mean standardized uptake value, metabolic tumor volume, total lesion glycolysis (TLG) and immune-organ SUVs were measured and the ratios calculated. Survival analyses used the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox regression. Results There were 91 death events (71.7%); the Kaplan-Meier median overall survival was 16.56 months, with 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival rates of 58.3%, 33.1%, and 28.1%, respectively. No significant independent association with overall survival was demonstrated for any of the primary-tumor or immune-organ PET/CT parameters; the SBR was lower in deceased patients (p=0.041) and showed a non-significant protective trend at the univariate level [hazard ratio (HR)=0.802 per 1 standard deviation (SD); 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.621-1.038; p=0.093)], which was not supported by cut-off-based or multivariable analyses. In the primary multivariable model, distant metastasis independently increased the hazard of death (HR=1.798; 95% CI 1.187-2.723; p=0.006), whereas TLG SLR, and BLR showed no independent significance. In the stage-adjusted model, advanced stage remained independently associated with OS (HR=4.403; p=0.001). Conclusion In this gastric adenocarcinoma cohort with a high proportion of advanced-stage disease, no independent association with overall survival was demonstrated for any of the evaluated tumor- or immune-organ PET/CT parameters; established clinicopathological factors showed stronger prognostic associations than the PET-derived parameters. The prognostic role of immune organ metabolism in gastric cancer should be evaluated in large prospective studies.

title: Integration of CURB-65 and CT Severity Score for Prognostic Prediction in Community-acquired Pneumonia.
abstract: Objective This study compared confusion, urea, respiratory rate, blood pressure, age ≥65 years (CURB-65) and computed tomography severity score (CTSS) for predicting 30-day mortality, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and length of hospital stay in patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and assessed whether CTSS added prognostic value to CURB-65. Material and methods This retrospective study included 456 adults with CT-confirmed CAP. CURB-65 and CTSS were calculated. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed for 30-day mortality and ICU admission, and area under the curve (AUC) values were compared using the DeLong test. Results For mortality prediction, the AUC values were 0.894 for CURB-65, 0.762 for mean CTSS, and 0.909 for the combined mortality model. The combined model did not significantly outperform CURB-65 ( P = 0.081). For ICU admission, the AUC values were 0.851, 0.716, and 0.881, respectively; the combined ICU model significantly outperformed CURB-65 ( P = 0.003). The mean CTSS was independently associated with mortality and ICU admission, but was not associated with length of hospital stay. Conclusion CURB-65 remained a strong and practical predictor of mortality and ICU admission in CAP. Mean CTSS provided additional prognostic information for mortality and ICU admission, but not for length of hospital stay. The combined mortality model did not significantly improve discrimination compared with CURB-65 alone, whereas the combined ICU model did significantly improve discrimination in predicting ICU admission.

title: Artificial Stone Silicosis: New Face of an Old Disease.
abstract: Artificial stone (AS) silicosis has emerged as a major global occupational health concern, challenging the perception of silicosis as a disease of the past. Driven by the fabrication of AS products containing high concentrations of crystalline silica (>90%), this rapidly progressive form disproportionately affects younger workers and develops after a much shorter exposure duration (median 7-19 years) than in classic silicosis. As cases continue to emerge worldwide, clinicians and occupational health practitioners are increasingly likely to encounter affected workers in clinical practice. This review provides a clinically focused synthesis of the current evidence on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and management of AS silicosis. Compared with traditional silicosis, the unique physicochemical properties of AS dust may amplify lung toxicity and promote a self-perpetuating inflammatory response. This frequently results in rapid development of progressive massive fibrosis, with disease progression often continuing after exposure cessation. Diagnosis is often delayed because of overlapping clinical features and the limited sensitivity of conventional screening tools, highlighting the importance of early clinical recognition, detailed occupational history-taking, and the use of high-resolution computed tomography where appropriate. Lung transplantation remains the only definitive treatment for advanced disease, underscoring the importance of prevention. Effective prevention requires strong workplace controls, systematic medical surveillance, and appropriate regulatory measures. Clinicians play a key role in early detection, patient education, and mandatory disease reporting. Coordinated action across clinical, occupational, and policy domains is essential to improve recognition, strengthen preventive measures, and avert further cases of this highly preventable occupational disease.

title: Robotic Parenchyma-Preserving Pancreatic Resection for Focal Congenital Hyperinsulinism in an Infant.
abstract: Background Robot-assisted surgery has been increasingly adopted over traditional laparoscopic and open procedures. However, its application in neonates and infants remains limited. Restricted space, delicate tissues, and the need for special instruments complicate its use. This case report describes the application of robot-assisted surgery in an infant with focal congenital hyperinsulinism. Materials and methods We describe the management of focal congenital hyperinsulinism in an infant using robotic surgery with indocyanine green injection, intraoperative ultrasound, and a suture-based retraction technique. Case description Herein, we present a case of an infant weighing less than 5 kg who underwent robotic surgery. The procedure was performed using the 3 arms of the da Vinci Xi robotic system and a suture-based intraoperative retraction technique. Intraoperative frozen sections confirmed the complete excision of the focal disease. Final histopathology revealed focal adenomatous hyperplasia. Intraoperatively, plasma glucose levels transiently increased after resection peaking at 23.1 mmol/L. Intravenous dextrose was discontinued. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the infant was discharged on postoperative day nine after tolerating full oral feeds. At follow-up in 8 months, the child remained euglycemic without any medical therapy or hypoglycemic episodes. Discussion This case demonstrates the feasibility of robotic-assisted parenchyma-preserving pancreatic resection in a 4.6-kg infant. Careful attention to operative planning and the use of adjuncts, such as indocyanine green fluorescence and intraoperative ultrasonography, is critical. Minimizing the number of additional ports and using suture-based retraction techniques can help achieve successful robotic surgery in this high-risk population.

title: AI-Assisted Volumetric Comparison of Parenchyma-Sparing Effect in Robotic Segmentectomy vs Lobectomy.
abstract: Background and objective In recent years, pulmonary segmentectomy has become a preferred treatment option for early-stage lung cancer. The primary factor encouraging clinicians to choose segmentectomy is the assumption of greater parenchymal preservation. In this study, we investigated the parenchyma-sparing effect of robotic pulmonary segmentectomy compared with robotic lobectomy using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted 3-dimensional (3D) volumetric analysis. Methods Preoperative and postoperative thoracic computed tomography scans of patients diagnosed with lung cancer between January 2022 and December 2025 who underwent robotic lobectomy or segmentectomy were analyzed using Synapse 3D software. Resected, remaining, expected, and measured lung volumes were calculated. Differences between predicted and measured values were analyzed using the independent-samples t test or the Mann-Whitney U test, depending on the data distribution. Results A total of 39 patients were included in the study. Lobectomy was performed in 21 patients, and segmentectomy in 18. The median resected lung volume was 360.5 mL (interquartile range [IQR]: 198-550) in the segmentectomy group and 896 mL (IQR: 599-1194) in the lobectomy group ( P < .001). The difference in expected remaining lung volume percentages between the lobectomy and segmentectomy groups was statistically significant ( P < .001), whereas the difference in measured postoperative remaining lung volumes was not statistically significant ( P = .1). Conclusion This pilot study demonstrated that robotic segmentectomy may not provide the expected parenchymal preservation advantage compared with lobectomy. Further prospective multicenter studies with larger cohorts are required.

title: Endovascular management of acute and chronic arterial mesenteric ischaemia: A narrative review of evidence informing interventional radiology treatment.
abstract: Mesenteric ischaemia is a potentially life-threatening vascular disorder caused by impaired intestinal perfusion, with treatment selection requiring consideration of clinical presentation, bowel viability and lesion anatomy. This narrative review examines evidence informing interventional radiology decisions in arterial acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) and chronic mesenteric ischaemia (CMI). MEDLINE/PubMed was searched from inception to December 31, 2025, supplemented by reference-list screening and targeted guideline searches. Qualitative evidence synthesis considered patient selection, study design, adjunctive treatments, outcomes and follow-up. In AMI, endovascular techniques can restore perfusion, but predominantly retrospective evidence does not establish superiority over surgery in bowel preservation or survival. For CMI requiring revascularisation, European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommend an initial endovascular approach, supported by Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe consensus-based guidance. Observational comparisons associate endovascular treatment with lower perioperative morbidity, and surgery with less symptom recurrence. By linking individual treatment decisions to society guidance and supporting studies, this review complements existing comprehensive reviews and guidance documents. It distinguishes formal recommendations and consensus-based practice from technical feasibility and demonstrated comparative patient benefit, while identifying unresolved questions concerning AMI reperfusion strategies and device selection, in addition to antithrombotic therapy and restenosis management in CMI.

title: Diagnostic performance of computed tomography-guided percutaneous bone biopsy in musculoskeletal oncology: A single-center cohort study.
abstract: Background Computed tomography guided percutaneous bone biopsy provides tissue for the assessment of suspected primary and secondary bone lesions. Diagnostic yield, concordance with subsequent diagnostic assessment, and adverse events describe different aspects of performance. Their interpretation depends on case selection, outcome definitions, and the completeness and independence of diagnostic verification. Aim To describe diagnostic yield, recorded diagnostic concordance, and complications in a retrospective single-center cohort of image-guided bone biopsies. title: Rickettsia rickettsii encephalitis in Brazilian spotted fever: a case report.
abstract: Brazilian spotted fever, caused by Rickettsia rickettsii, is a life-threatening tick-borne disease endemic to southeastern Brazil and is associated with high mortality when treatment is delayed. Central nervous system involvement poses a particular diagnostic challenge because of nonspecific early symptoms and frequent misdiagnosis as dengue or leptospirosis. We report a case illustrating characteristic neuroimaging findings and therapeutic considerations in rickettsial encephalitis. We describe the clinical course, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings, serologic results, and treatment response in a 23-year-old man who presented with febrile encephalopathy in an endemic region of Brazil. The patient had a five-day history of fever, erythematous macules, and progressive encephalopathy. CSF analysis showed elevated protein and lymphocytic pleocytosis. MRI showed T2/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery hyperintensities with restricted diffusion involving the bilateral corticospinal tracts and the splenium of the corpus callosum, forming a "boomerang" pattern. Clinical improvement followed initiation of empirical doxycycline and pulse methylprednisolone. Serologic testing supported the diagnosis of R. rickettsii infection with a positive immunoglobulin M titer of 1:512. Follow-up MRI showed near-complete lesion resolution at 4 months, with a residual splenial lesion persisting at 18 months. This case illustrates the importance of recognizing characteristic MRI patterns, including the "starry sky" and "boomerang" signs, as diagnostic clues in rickettsial encephalitis, even when the classic triad is incomplete. Early empirical doxycycline remains critical for neurologic outcomes, and adjunctive corticosteroids may have a role in selected cases when immune-mediated central nervous system injury is suspected.

title: Focal Hypoganglionosis-Associated Adult-Onset Megacolon: A Localized Enteric Neuropathy Distinct From Chronic Intestinal Pseudo-Obstruction.
abstract: Adult-onset megacolon is a heterogeneous disorder traditionally classified within the spectrum of idiopathic megacolon or chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction (CIPO). However, accumulating evidence suggests that a subset of patients demonstrates distinct clinicopathologic features characterized by localized motor dysfunction resulting in focal colonic narrowing, proximal megacolon, and localized hypoganglionosis. In this review, we refer to this phenotype as focal hypoganglionosis-associated adult-onset megacolon (FHAM). Clinically, patients with FHAM frequently present with severe chronic constipation, progressive abdominal distension and pain, nausea, vomiting, recurrent sub-occlusive or pseudo-obstructive episodes, and repeated decompressive interventions. Computed tomography typically demonstrates proximal megacolon with focal functional narrowing, whereas small bowel motility is preserved despite severe colonic dilatation. Histopathologic studies additionally demonstrated inflammatory ganglionitis associated with CD3-positive lymphocytic infiltration within the myenteric plexus. Molecular and physiologic studies of resected colonic tissue further revealed impaired neuromuscular signaling and smooth muscle contractility within the affected segment, suggesting localized enteric neuropathy as a potential pathogenic mechanism. Importantly, accumulating evidence suggests that patients with FHAM generally demonstrate favorable long-term outcomes following adequate surgical resection compared with patients with CIPO, including markedly lower rates of postoperative reoperation (2.5% vs. 66.7% with CIPO) and long-term total parenteral nutrition requirement (0% vs. 46.2% with CIPO). In summary, current evidence supports the concept that FHAM in adults represents a surgically remediable localized enteric neuropathic phenotype that can be clinically distinguished from classical CIPO. Recognition of this phenotype is clinically important because timely diagnosis and appropriate surgical intervention may substantially improve long-term outcomes.

title: HPV Detection by RT-PCR in Laryngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Correlation with p16 Expression, Histopathology, and Prognosis.
abstract: Objective The aim of the study was to determine HPV incidence among laryngeal squamous cell carcinomas (LSCC) using HPV E6/E7 mRNA RT-PCR and to compare diagnostic capabilities of p16 immunohistochemistry against it. With the data gathered, the relationship between HPV status, pathological and clinical parameters will be assessed. Material and methods This retrospective, single-centred study included 112 laryngectomy cases tested for HPV E6/E7 mRNA using RT-PCR, which detects transcripts of 14 high-risk HPV types, and additionally identifies the presence of HPV 16 and 18/45-specific transcripts. p16 protein immunohistochemistry was also performed, and overall results were compared with clinical and pathological data. Results p16 immunoreactivity was observed in 18 cases (16%). In one case, more than 70% of the tumour cells exhibited strong staining. The p16 immunohistochemistry (IHC) score was above 6/9 in 5 cases (28% of p16-positive cases, 4% of all cases). Despite p16 reactivity, none of the cases demonstrated transcriptionally active HPV with RT-PCR tests. The RT-PCR analysis result was positive for HPV type 16 in one case, with no p16 immunoreactivity observed in the tumour cells. Conclusion In our study, the findings suggest that HPV has a minimal effect on LSCC carcinogenesis in Türkiye. Our findings suggest that p16 immunohistochemistry may not be a suitable surrogate marker for HPV detection in LSCC. Additionally, p16 IHC positivity was associated with decreased survival. This suggests that p16 expression could potentially be used as a prognostic marker, although its clinical significance requires fur-ther validation.
